News.title: Grim moment Iranian crowds gather to see execution – as Trump threatens to ‘easily take out’ regime’s Pickaxe nuke lair
News.content:
HUGE crowds gathered in Iran as the ruthless regime publicly executed two men for taking part in protests that rocked the country earlier this year.

It comes as US President Donald Trump threatened to unleash fresh strikes on Iran over fears the regime has stockpiled uranium in its Pickaxe Mountain nuclear lair.



Footage shows scaffolding and a crane erected in Alikhani Square, in Isfahan, as a swarm of people surround the scene ahead of the hangings.

“The death sentences of Abolfazl Sepahi Badjani and Amir Hossein Safari Hosseinabadi have been carried out“, Iran’s official news agency IRNA announced on Tuesday.



The pair were among 12 men sentenced on charges of taking part in the killing of security force members in the same square on January 8.

Another two in the same trial had already been executed.



On Monday night clashes broke out at the square between security forces and protesters hoping to stop the executions, local media Iranintl reports.

“They chased people through the alleyways of Isfahan last night, they did not even spare a thought for those mothers” one witness told the outlet.



Rights groups have raised concerns over allegations of coerced confessions, closed court hearings and the defendants’ young ages.

At least 24 people have been executed in connection with the January protests so far, according to UN experts.

Nationwide anti-government protests sparked by the high cost of living erupted across the country in January.



The unrest spiralled into widespread anti-government demonstrations that were met with the biggest crackdown in the history of the Islamic Republic.

Security forces killed thousands of protesters, filling the streets with piles of body bags.

Trump threatened to intervene at the time, telling protesters that “help is on the way”.



The US and Israel began airstrikes on the rogue nation in February to stop the killings and prevent Tehran obtaining a nuclear weapon.

The war in Iran was paused in June after Tehran and Washington thrashed out a truce agreement.

Washington suspended a two-week campaign of renewed strikes on Saturday for fresh negotiations but Trump threatened to resume attacks if talks fall through.

Amid the high-stakes meetings, Israel has reportedly shared new secret intelligence with Trump on Iran’s nuclear activity at Pickaxe Mountain.

Tehran allegedly transferred thousands of uranium-enrichment centrifuges into the site after the 12-day war in June 2025, when US and Israeli strikes pummelled Iran’s main nuclear sites.



Today Trump told Fox News: “We have the greatest cameras in the world focused on [it]…I know exactly what’s going on at Pickaxe, it’s not a big problem.

“We took out their nuclear sites, and we’ll have to take out Pickaxe if we don’t make a deal. If we don’t make a deal, we’ll take it out very easily.”

The highly fortified Pickaxe Mountain lair lies more than 300 feet beneath Kolang Mountain, near the Natanz nuclear facility.

The head of the UN’s nuclear watchdog said last year: “It is obvious it is in a place where numerous and important activities related to the programme are taking place.”

Trump has previously left the site untouched while bombing Iran’s other major nuclear bunkers.



But last week he warned the US would strike the area “pretty soon” and “very heavily.”

News.title: Dexter fanatic who chopped up his two roommates before scattering their remains by cabin in woods GUILTY of murder
News.content:
GRISLY KILLING Dexter fanatic who chopped up his two roommates before scattering their remains by cabin in woods GUILTY of murder

A DEXTER fanatic has been found guilty of murdering his two roommates after he chopped up their bodies and scattered the remains by his woodland cabin.

James Desborough killed Daniel Coleman, 43, and Claudio Aquilino, 57, after meeting them at a homeless residence in Newquay, Cornwall.



The 40-year-old then dismembered their bodies in Paramoor Woods, near Sticker in Cornwall and tried to burn and bury their remains.

Desborough also stole their money and used Daniel’s cash to treat himself to a “large beef roast” after chopping him up.



While he was awaiting trial for the double murder, evil Desborough was convicted of strangling 65-year-old cellmate Steven Kempster to death at HMP Exeter.

The monster has now been found guilty of murdering Claudio between April 17 and July 7 last year and killing Daniel between June 2 and July 7 last year.



He previously pleaded guilty to preventing the lawful burial of the two men’s bodies.

Winchester Crown Court heard around the time of the killings, Desborough messaged a pal describing himself as “absolutely bloodthirsty real hostile fuming spitting feathers”.



The text was dated on May 30, 2025 – the date Claudio became a missing person.

Chillingly, a week earlier, Desborough had told Daniel he was a “f***ing r****d” and warned him: “Don’t take me for a mug, boy.”

They had fallen out over Daniel’s relationship with Hannah Cresswell, with whom Desborough had had an affair.

Ahmed Hossain KC, prosecuting, said parts of Daniel’s dismembered body, including his torso, legs and feet, were later found in a shallow grave.

Daniel’s DNA was discovered on an axe that was hanging from a tree nearby, jurors heard.



Claudio’s shallow grave was found 18 metres away.

Cops discovered 1,900 burnt bone fragments – belonging to Claudio – at a stream nearby.

A “piece of flesh” – also from the victim – was in the water, and a search party also found “two pieces of unburnt scapula”.



Police also seized a large number of handwritten notes in the woodland cabin, the court heard.

One said: “I know I’m a killer, ready to kill and execute any predators.”

Another included “detailed travel plans and intent to leave the UK”.

This note mentioned a “shuffle bag liner”, “bodies buried”, “new disguise”, “new burner phone” and “safe house”.

Mr Hossain said Desborough was a fan of the hit TV show Dexter – in which the lead character is a serial killer who dismembers people.



The killer told a forensic biologist involved in the woodland searches that he “particularly enjoyed the dismemberment scenes” in the show.

RECOMMENDED STORIES

Desborough confessed he “lost all grip on reality” and tried to hide their bodies – insisting he only found them dead on his land and that he didn’t kill them.

He will be sentenced on a later date.

News.title: Two men stabbed & woman punched after being dragged from car in Tesco car park as cops hunt gang on e-bikes
News.content:
SHOCK ATTACK Two men stabbed & woman punched after being dragged from car in Tesco car park as cops hunt gang on e-bikes

TWO men have been rushed to hospital with stab wounds after they were dragged from a car by a gang on e-bikes in a Tesco car park.

The pair were travelling in a black Hyundai Tucson when they were allegedly targeted by a group of men riding electric bikes and a quad bike in Billingham, County Durham.



The alleged assault, which took place around 9.35pm on Monday, July 28, saw the gang drive their electric vehicles at the Hyundai, causing damage to the car.

The group of men are said to have dragged the occupants from the vehicle and launched an assault.



A woman, the driver of the Hyundai, is reported to have been taken from the car and punched in the face.

Meanwhile, two men sitting in the back of the car were also allegedly pulled out and stabbed in the abdomen and sides.

Both male victims were taken to hospital for treatment, though their injuries are not thought to be life-threatening.

A fourth man, who was sitting in the passenger seat of the car, was not hurt in the incident.

The Tesco, which is open daily from 6am to midnight, was closed to customers after police arrived.

Detectives at Cleveland Police have launched an investigation into the assault and are appealing for witnesses to come forward.



A spokesperson for Cleveland Police said: “Anyone who witnessed the incident and has not yet spoken with officers, or anyone with footage of the incident or the quad and e-bikes riding away, is asked to call 101 quoting reference number 148971.”

News.title: Man, 60, fighting for his life after being hit by double-decker bus in high street
News.content:
A MAN in his 60s is fighting for his life in a trauma unit after being hit by a double-decker bus on a busy high street.

Police and paramedics rushed to the scene in Hackney, London, this morning after receiving reports of a collision between a bus and a pedestrian.



A man in his 60s was found on Kingsland Road High Street and was rushed to a major trauma centre in an ambulance.

The London Ambulance Service said ambulance crews, a paramedic in a fast response car, an incident response officer and a trauma team in a car from London’s Air Ambulance were sent to the scene.



Cops closed the road as an investigation into the horror got underway with a cordon currently still in place around the scene.

No arrests have been made at this time, the Met Police confirmed.

Images show the aftermath of the smash with police tape blocking off the road and emergency vehicles swarming the area.

Several officers can be seen guarding the scene as a probe into the collision continues.

A number 149 bus to London Bridge remains stopped in the middle of the deserted road.

A London Ambulance Service spokesperson said: “We were called at 10:09am today [28 July] to reports of a road traffic collision on Kingsland High Street, Hackney, E8.



“We sent ambulance crews, a paramedic in a fast response car and an incident response officer to the scene.

“We also dispatched a trauma team in a car from London’s Air Ambulance.

“The first paramedic arrived on the scene in less than two minutes. We treated a patient and took him to a major trauma centre by road.”

A Met Police spokesperson said: “Police were called at 10:12hrs on Tuesday, 28 July to reports of a collision involving a bus and a pedestrian on Kingsland High Street, Hackney.

“Officers are at the scene and Kingsland High Street is currently closed between Crossway and Sandringham Road.



“The pedestrian, a man aged 60, was taken to hospital where his injuries were deemed to be life-threatening and life-changing.

“No arrests have been made and an investigation is underway to establish what took place.”

News.title: Dad shoots wife and their six children, 5 to 15, dead before setting fire to their home and turning gun on himself
News.content:
A MAN shot dead his wife and their six children – then turned the gun on himself – before setting fire to their Michigan home.

The bodies of Kristopher and Amanda Karolkiewicz and their six kids, aged five to 15, were found in their upmarket home in Grand Haven Township.



Ottawa County Sheriff’s Capt. Jake Sparks told a press conference that all victims had been shot.

“The investigation at this point shows that this is a murder-suicide, with the fire being started after the murders,” Sparks said.



The fire also seems to have been set intentionally in multiple parts of the house after the killings, but officials still are investigating this, the sheriff’s office said.

“This is an unspeakable tragedy that we may never fully understand,” Sheriff Eric DeBoer said in a statement.

Police were called to the scene after receiving reports of white smoke pouring from the building.

At the time, Sparks described the grim scene as “complicated”.

An elementary school substitute teacher, Amanda was described as a “kind and devoted soul” who loved her family and her students.

Her mother and stepfather, Becky and Steve Lawwill, said in a statement: “We treasured every moment we had with her and her six children, and words cannot adequately address our devastation.”



A January post by the local school district said the teacher “went above and beyond for students, especially when they’re having a hard day, responding with empathy, patience, and care.”

Amanda and Kris met at work at a beverage company in 2008 and began dating that summer, according to a parenting-oriented blog that she kept over a decade ago. The two married in August 2009.

They had their first child in 2011, which she hailed as “the best day of my life (so far)”.



Two more sons followed over the next four years, as she shifted from a banking job to a part-time position at a local insurance agency and later stopped working outside the home.

The couple later adopted two daughters and had another biological son.

Heartbroken relatives have paid tribute to their late loved ones.

Amanda’s sister, Molly Cessna, said: “Everything’s just blurry. Please continue to pray, friends. please continue to pray as we try and piece everything together.

“Our hearts are utterly shattered. Tragic doesn’t even touch it.”



For those having thoughts of suicide, there are resources available. Call the National Suicide Prevention Lifeline at 1-800-273-8255 (TALK). If you or someone you know is affected by any of the issues raised in this story, call or text the 988 Suicide & Crisis Lifeline at 988, chat on 988lifeline.org, or text Crisis Text Line at 741741.

News.title: Polanski’s sick anti-Farage post just days after Ann Widdecombe’s brutal murder lays bare rank hypocrisy of Left
News.content:
IT DOESN’T take much to imagine what would happen if Nigel Farage jokingly posted an image of Green Party leader Zack Polanski being strung up from a lamp post.

The police would lose no time in sending a dozen officers to his home to arrest him.



The Left would go into overdrive, saying that the ‘chilling’ image proved that Reform UK was just one step removed from the Ku Klux Klan.

Words and pictures, we would be reminded, have consequences, and nothing less than a long prison sentence for Farage would do.



But when it is the other way around?

We know the answer because at the weekend, Zack Polanski shared with his 700,000 Instagram followers an image of a man wearing a t-shirt bearing the image of a guillotine and the words “we’re only making plans for Nigel”.

The photo was taken at a Green party rally at the weekend.

The police say they are investigating the incident, but don’t expect any action to be taken against Polanski.

As for the Left, the incident seems hardly to have registered on their radar screens.

I don’t think for a moment that Polanski really wants Farage beheaded. But surely, following the murder of Ann Widdecombe a fortnight ago, as well the murders of MPs Jo Cox and David Amess, he ought to know that joking about violence towards public figures is extremely dangerous.



It is, as Farage has said, a form of incitement. It only takes one deranged individual to take it as an instruction and we could be dealing with yet another political murder.

Green party members are developing a reputation for disgusting comments on social media.

Tina Ion, who stood in Newcastle in May’s local elections posted a picture of an industrial shredding machine along with the words ‘zionist juicer’.



One of her colleagues, Philip Brookes, posted an image of a torn Israeli flag with a swastika behind, as well as suggesting that thanks to the war in Gaza it “takes serious effort not to be a tiny bit antisemitic”.

The party withdrew support from both candidates, but does it not have a vetting procedure?

Sadly, Polanski’s Greens are evolving into an extreme Islamist party in green clothes.

The Left doesn’t see any of this because to them, the ‘Far Right’ – a definition which in their minds includes anyone backed Brexit, opposes mass migration or who thinks that the government should live within its means — has a monopoly on violence.

Everything that right wing figures say is construed as incitement.



Remember how the Left instantly blamed Jo Cox’s murder – by a right wing extremist – on the Brexit campaign?

Or how the actions of Darren Osborne, who drove a van into a crowd outside Finsbury Park Mosque in 2017, were quickly blamed on the tabloids?

Actually, at his trial it was revealed that he was spurred into action after watching a BBC documentary.



Even more absurdly, Labour MP Kate Osborne (no relation) tried to blame the Islamist attack on a Pride event in Berlin last weekend on Reform UK, claiming that the party was culpable because it was part of an “escalation of hate”.

How different it was after Ann Widdecombe’s murder when we were told not to speculate on the killer’s motives.

After David Amess’ murder it quickly emerged that he had been killed by an Islamist terrorist, but you would hardly have known from some of the coverage, which sought to blame the crime on a general coarsening of political debate.

The Left didn’t want us speculating on anything to do with Southport killer, Axel Rudakubana, the British-born son of Rwandan refugees who was later found to have al-Qaeda materials in his bedroom.

Within hours, Keir Starmer was on the television trying to turn the whole thing into a story about the Far Right.



Lucy Connolly, a child-minder married to a Conservative councillor, was quickly arrested and later jailed for tweeting about setting light to migrant hostels.

I am not going to defend Connolly, even if her 31 month sentence was over the top. What she wrote could indeed be taken as incitement, even if she didn’t intend it that way.

But what a different story it was when the murder of George Floyd in Minneapolis in 2020 was followed by riots.

The protests were described by the BBC as ‘largely peaceful’, even when 14 police officers were injured in Whitehall. Starmer ignored the left-wing violence and took the knee.

Remember when comedian Jo Brand, commenting on an incident in which Nigel Farage had a milk shake thrown over him, said “I’m thinking, why bother with a milkshake when you could get some battery acid”.



A pathetic BBC response after multiple complaints judged that Brand “went beyond what was appropriate” but dismissed any notion that it constituted incitement. The police showed no interest.

The Left, and the Greens in particular, seem to think they are all love and peace.

RECOMMENDED STORIES

The reality is that they can give the Far Right a good run for its money when it comes to violence and hate speech.

Polanski’s inability to see this shows, once again, why he is unfit for public office.

News.title: Speedboat killer Jack Shepherd pinned girlfriend down and beat her with BBQ tongs after she burnt pizza in abuse hell
News.content:
SPEEDBOAT killer Jack Shepherd pinned down and beat his new girlfriend with BBQ tongs in a sickening campaign of abuse.

The vile 39-year-old attacked the vulnerable woman twice after he was released from prison.



Shepherd was previously jailed for killing Charlotte Brown, 24, who was thrown from his boat on the River Thames in December 2015.

He was released from prison in January 2024 and met a woman known only as Ms X shortly after, court documents claim.



Shepherd pinned down the woman and punched her “several times causing bruising to her arm and top of leg” in February 2025.

He also flew into a rage when his partner burnt a pizza so struck her in the chest with barbecue tongs in June 2025 causing a permanent scar.



He appeared at Isleworth Crown Court today where he admitted the two counts of assault occasioning actual bodily harm and damaging property.

Prosecutors agreed to drop two other allegations, of controlling or coercive behaviour and intentional suffocation.

According to court documents, Shepherd and Ms X were in a relationship that continued even after she was told by the police about his history.



By the end of 2024, Shepherd became violent and coercive towards Ms X, who complained to the police.

The woman accused him of “belittling” her with jibes about her weight and age, and accused her of flirting with other men.

As part of the controlling or coercive behaviour charge, which was dropped by prosecutors, she also claimed he had mentioned a violent former cellmate and allegedly told her it would be her “last day” if she said anything bad to his probation officer.

The documents said he was arrested on August 5, 2025, and recalled to custody a month later after his licence was revoked.



Shepherd was jailed for six years in April 2019, for manslaughter by gross negligence.

But the following year, he had almost three months slashed from his sentence.

On the night Charlotte died, Shepherd tried to impress her with a late-night trip past the Houses of Parliament after dinner at the Shard.

He had been drinking heavily before the tragedy, while English literature graduate Charlotte barely touched a drop on their first date.

Charlotte, who died shortly after hitting the river from cold water immersion, could be heard screaming: “Oh my God, you’re going so fast”.

Shockingly, Shepherd fled the UK before he could face justice in person and spent ten months on the run.

It was while he was hiding in Georgia that the chilling truth behind the champagne Casanova began to emerge.

Police discovered Shepherd had bought the boat from Gumtree to “pull” and had taken ten other women for rides before the fatal crash.



Shepherd, who got married and had a child after the crash, eventually handed himself into local authorities in Georgia and even tried protesting his innocence in front of TV cameras.

Smirking as he surrendered, he insisted it was a “tragic accident”.

News.title: Tragic new details emerge after teen, 15, & mum died while swimming with relatives – as boy, 7, still fighting for life
News.content:
A TEENAGER and mother tragically died while swimming at the beach with four other relatives.

Cops have confirmed the identities of the woman and girl who drowned, while a seven-year-old boy remains in hospital in critical condition.



Shelina Rahman, 41, and her daughter Sameeha, 15, died on Mersea Island beach on July 22.

The pair had travelled to the West Essex seaside spot from their home in London to spend the day at the beach along with some family members.



The group had been enjoying swimming in the sea when the boy reportedly got into difficulty.

It is understood that the mother and daughter sprang into action to help save their relative, but both tragically died.



The young boy was flown to hospital where he remains in a critical condition.

The investigation is being led by Detective Chief Inspector Al Pitcher, who said: “We are continuing to support Shelina and Sameeha’s family through this extremely difficult time.



“They had been enjoying a family day at the beach together when this tragedy happened.

“We are working to establish the circumstances which led up to this incident and our enquiries are ongoing.

“We have spoken to a number of key witnesses and will continue to do so over the coming days and will work with partners including the fire service, local council, and coastguard.”

Chief Inspector Michelle Sparks, the District Commander for Colchester, said: “I want to thank the community for their response to this incident.

“There were members of the public who rushed to help the family and I want to thank them for their courage and selflessness.



“Since this tragic incident we have also seen an outpouring of support and sympathy.

“At times of tragedy you get to see how strong a community is, and we have a fantastic community on Mersea Island, and across the Colchester district.”

Essex Police have asked anyone who was in the area at the time and has information or footage which could assist their investigation to contact them on 101 and quote incident 1090 of 22 July.

The cops scrambled to the beach at around 5.30pm last Wednesday where they reportedly found the boy in a coma.

Two other family members sustained non-life threatening injuries, and the boy was rushed to hospital.



A source told The Sun how the grandmother of Sameeha watched her get dragged out by the tide.

RECOMMENDED STORIES

They said: “The grandmother watched as she lost her daughter and her granddaughter in front of her eyes.

“She was completely helpless. She has not stopped crying since it happened.”

News.title: Are you worried your holiday plans could be affected by France and Spain wildfires?
News.content:
Are you worried your holiday plans could be affected by France and Spain wildfires?

British tourists in a region devastated by wildfires are being urged 'do not come' as French president Emmanuel Macron said the crisis was the worst of its kind 'since World War II'

View 2 Images Tourists are being urged not to come to the fire-hit region of Gironde, France (Image: AFP via Getty Images)

British holidaymakers are being warned not to cancel their holidays abroad until they hear from their travel provider after officials in a fire-hit region urged tourists to 'stay away'.

‌



Over 330,000 people have been driven from their homes and accommodation as flames continued to tear across southwest France and northern Spain - with temperatures set to rocket above 35C again this week.

‌



Sophie Brocas, prefect of the French department of Gironde where the the majority of the evacuations have taken place, warned: "We urge tourists not to come to this region, at least until the situation is under control."

‌



The Foreign Office has not yet issued a 'do not travel' warning for the affected regions - with Brits instead asked to check ahead with their accommodation or package holiday provider.

As a 'do not travel' warning isn't in place, anyone who cancels their holiday themselves could face losing their right to a refund and ability to claim from their holiday insurance, experts say.

‌



A spokesperson for ABTA, the industry body which represents UK travel agents, tour operators, and the wider industry, told the Mirror: "If you have booked a package holiday to a destination affected by a wildfire your tour operator will be closely monitoring the situation and if the holiday cannot be provided or has been significantly effected, they will offer an alternative trip or a full refund for the cost of the package.

"However, if this is not the case and you chose yourself to cancel, you will almost certainly incur a cancellation fee."

"If you have booked independently, you should always check with your accommodation provider to see whether your accommodation is available and if not what their refund policy is, as if you do not, this may affect any potential claim you make on your travel insurance."

‌



View 2 Images Two cars destroyed by a wildfire in El Tiemblo, 50 miles west of Madrid (Image: AFP via Getty Images)

Popular holiday destinations in the affected Gironde region of France include Arcachon, Bordeaux and Fontainebleau forest.

Avila, Toledo, Valencia and Castellon are among the tourist favourites under wildfire warnings in Spain.

‌



France and Spain are the two most popular overseas destinations for British holidaymakers. In 2024, UK residents made approximately 17.8 million visits to Spain, and 9.3 million visits to France, according to Foreign Office figures.

In his latest comments today, President Emmanuel Macron said the fire was France’s worst fire-related crisis "since World War II" - and warned that a freak weather event was complicating firefighting efforts.

Speaking from outside an office building being used to co-ordinate the emergency response, he said: "We’re facing a completely unprecedented fire.

Article continues below

"We had some events that we have never experienced before. First, we know that the Landes and Gascogne forest is extremely difficult to control - we experienced this in 2022.

"But on top of that comes extreme drought. Added to this, on top of all these factors and climate conditions, we are now seeing so-called pyrocumulonimbus clouds, which are real 'fire clouds' capable of carrying the fire much further."

News.title: Mum of missing sailor begs 'Frankenstein' killer to come clean about his disappearance
News.content:
Mum of missing sailor begs 'Frankenstein' killer to come clean about his disappearance

EXCLUSIVE: Margaret Parkes today issued a direct plea to 'Frankenstein' killer Allan Grimson in a desperate bid to find out what happened to her son, Simon Parkes

View 6 Images Simon's mother, Margaret, previously described Grimson as a "psychopath" who should never be freed (Image: SWNS)

The mother of a sailor missing for almost 40 years today issued a direct plea to the "Frankenstein" killer feared to have murdered him, begging: "Tell me what you did to my son."

‌



Margaret Parkes, 80, is adamant radio operator Simon fell victim to evil Allan Grimson, 66, when HMS Illustrious docked in Gibraltar in December 1986. Detectives investigating Simon's disappearance closed the probe into Grimson last December after drawing a blank.

‌



But Margaret says she is convinced the double killer - who was found guilty on Monday of sexually assaulting four men and boys - was behind her son's disappearance. And she says she still hopes for justice after nearly 40 years despite Grimson denying involvement in Simon's disappearance.

‌



View 6 Images Simon's family have spent nearly four decades searching for closure but are convinced he was another victim of serial killer Grimson (Image: PA)

In a direct message to Grimson, Margaret said: "Please tell us what happened to Simon." Calling for police to reopen the investigation, she added: "How do you get in to the head of a man like that? We want him to tell us what he knows, where Simon's body is, we would want that, but he's in denial now. All these years we've done all we can to find out information and keep the investigation open."

Grimson - nicknamed the Frankenstein Killer, due to his 6ft 2in frame and large forehead - was jailed for life in 2001 for murdering two young men who served with Simon on aircraft carrier Illustrious. He was convicted of battering to death Nicholas Wright, 18, of Leicestershire, and barman Sion Jenkins, 20, of Newbury, Berkshire.

‌



Grimson - who once claimed murder was "better than sex" - had invited the two Navy seamen to his flat and killed both with a baseball bat before dumping their bodies on two dates exactly a year apart in the 1990s. That date was December 12th - the same date that Simon vanished.

View 6 Images Grimson - nicknamed the Frankenstein Killer, due to his 6ft 2in frame and large forehead - was jailed for two murders in 2001 (Image: PA Archive/PA Images)

As he was sentenced in 2001, the judge branded Grimson a “serial killer in nature if not by number”. Yesterday he was found guilty of 13 offences against four other men and boys, including a 14-year-old, in the 1990s. Winchester Crown Court heard he told police one of his sex attack victims was "lucky" to be alive because he would have killed him if his friend was not sleeping on the sofa.

‌



He brought the teenager to his flat in Portsmouth, Hampshire, and sexually assaulted him - weeks before his killing spree. Grimson is said to have told police in 1999: "If you're going to rape somebody, to get away with it, kill it. And that's the only way you can do that."

For more than four decades Grimson has been linked to Simon's disappearance but has never been prosecuted. Grimson was serving on board the HMS Illustrious aircraft carrier at the same time as Simon.

View 6 Images Nicholas Wright, 18, was bludgeoned to death with a baseball bat after rejecting Grimson's his sexual advances (Image: PA Archive/PA Images)

‌



Now Margaret says she prays for a resolution so an inquest can be held and she can get answers about her son's disappearance. She says she has spent more than half her life in limbo and now hopes she can be issued with a death certificate if a coroner in Gibraltar is able to proceed.

She said: "I was very disappointed that the investigation was dropped. Now we want to have an inquest so we can also be given a death certificate after nearly 40 years. We want someone to say that Simon is dead.

"I'm 80 now so we probably don't have much longer if you think of it that way. And I want the investigation to be reopened so Grimson can be prosecuted and we can get justice. We want answers. We've been submerged in this for 40 years, it's always there and it's always been a feeling of helplessness. It's so painful."

‌



View 6 Images Sion Jenkins, 20, was murdered in the same Portsmouth flat where Grimson killed Nicholas (Image: PA Archive/PA Images)

Police have carried out a string of searches in Gibraltar including at a cemetery and in a car park. Grimson has always denied being involved in Simon's disappearance.

Six years ago, the Parole Board recommended Grimson be moved to an open prison as a first step towards being freed on licence. But his barrister, John Femi-Ola KC, said during his trial that Grimson’s chance of parole had been deliberately “stymied” when police began reinvestigating his contacts with four men and the Crown Prosecution Service gave the go-ahead for him to be charged.

‌



Mr Mr Femi-Ola told a jury at Winchester crown court that in 2020 the Parole Board recommended transferring Grimson to an open prison. The barrister described this as a “huge step” for Grimson, but said the authorities stepped in, approaching the four young males.

View 6 Images In 2024 British cops travelled to Gibraltar to carry out a search for missing Simon Parkes the Town Range car park (Image: RICHARD ATKINS/SOLARPIX.COM)

Mr Femi-Ola said that when police contacted one of the alleged victims, he was hesitant about making a fresh complaint and asked what it would achieve. The officer replied: “If successful it would mean his parole is denied.”

‌



During Grimson’s trial in 2001, one psychiatrist called him a psychopath and the most complex of over 250 murderers they’d met. Grimson - who once claimed murder was "better than sex" - has since been diagnosed as suffering from a severe personality disorder - The same as serial killer Dennis Nilsen.

As it cannot be treated, Grimson has served his sentence in prison, rather than being admitted to a hospital such as Broadmoor.

TIMELINE

December 12, 1986: Simon Parkes, from Bristol, vanishes after the the ship he was serving on, HMS Illustrious, docks in Gibraltar. The 18-year-old radio operator failed to return after a night out with crewmates, leaving his passport, belongings and Christmas presents on board the ship. He never returned and the ship returned to Portsmouth without him. Allan Grimson is serving aboard the aircraft carrier at the same time.

‌



December 12, 1997: Grimson bludgeons Nicholas Wright, 18, to death with a baseball bat after Wright rejected his sexual advances. The monster slices Nicholas' ear off with a diving knife, before slitting his throat. The next day, Grimson wraps Nicholas' naked body up – later telling police he felt a “tingling” sensation while doing so. He then dumps the naval rating’s mutilated body in a ditch.

December 12, 1988: Grimson attacks and rapes Sion Jenkins, 20, in the same Portsmouth flat where he killed Nicholas before tying him up and putting him in a bathtub. As Sion begs to go home, Grimson beats him to death with a bat before dumping his body by the side of the A32. Sion's body is discovered four miles (6.44km) from Nicholas' at the side of country lanes north of Winchester in December 1999. Grimson confesses to his crimes in excruciating detail, telling police in a 1999 interview: "If you’re going to rape somebody, to get away with it, kill it.”

April 5, 2001: Grimson is jailed for life for Sion's and Nicholas' murders. The judge recommends that he serve a minimum of 22 years, telling him he was a "serial killer in all but numbers". This sentence was increased to 25 years by the then Home Secretary. In 2008, Grimson won a reduction in his life sentence by three years. Following Grimson's conviction, Hampshire Police re-open the investigation into Simon's disappearance.

‌



June 8, 2003: Three detectives and a naval police officer return to Gibraltar to search for clues and spend a week investigating Simon's disappearance.

December 2, 2019 - A week-long search is launched by detectives who carry out a dig at Gibraltar's Trafalgar Cemetery.

August 7, 2023 - Nine officers travel to Gibraltar and carry out a small amount of excavation work at the Town Range car park as they "followed a potential further line of enquiry".

‌



January 19, 2024 - Police carry out further digs at the Town Range car park but fail to find any new information.

July 4, 2025: Grimson - whose sentence expired on December 20 2021 - is denied his freedom. The Parole Board rejects his application on public safety grounds, with Simon's mother saying: "As a family, we are going through a life sentence not knowing what happened to Simon or where he is buried. It is only right, at least until he gives up that information, that he suffers the same."

December 30, 2025: Police announce they are ending their investigation into Simon's disappearance. Hampshire and Isle of Wight Constabulary reveal, following the advice of the Crown Prosecution Service, that the investigation would be filed unless further information came to light.

Article continues below

July 17, 2026: Grimson is found guilty of 13 offences against four men and boys, including a 14-year-old, in the 1990s. His trial is told that he told police in 1999: "If you're going to rape somebody, to get away with it, kill it. And that's the only way you can do that." He will be sentenced in November.

News.title: Trump live: Zelensky and Netanyahu at White House as Donald set to quiz Putin
News.content:
Donald Trump is holding crucial talks at the White House with Volodymyr Zelensky and Benjamin Netanyahu, who are both in Washington DC for the funeral of Senator Lindsey Graham

Donald Trump is set to hold crucial talks with Volodymyr Zelensky and Benjamin Netanyahu at the White House today - just days after Zelensky accused Russia of helping Iran target US troops.

Both the Ukrainian president and Israeli prime minister are in Washington DC to attend the funeral of Senator Lindsey Graham, who died earlier this month aged 71.

Zelensky has said he plans to discuss strengthening Ukraine's anti-ballistic missile defences with Trump. It comes after the Ukrainian leader said on Saturday that Kyiv has intelligence indicating Russia shared satellite imagery with Tehran, enabling Iran to target US military bases in the Middle East. Trump said that he will "find out if that's true" and "ask Putin about it".

After meeting Zelensky, Trump will hold talks with Netanyahu - marking their first in-person meeting since the US-Israeli war on Iran began on February 28.

News.title: France wildfires map shows vast infernos as thousands of tourists told to leave
News.content:
France wildfires map shows vast infernos as thousands of tourists told to leave

Maps show the areas of south-west France still affected by raging wildfires as almost 4,000 more people have been evacuated from tourist sites in Lacanau

View 3 Images Flames have ripped through the countryside near Bordeaux (Image: Gengis Quidu-MPP/SIPA/Shutterstock)

New maps show the dramatic scale of wildfires still raging in south-west France after almost 4,000 more people were evacuated from tourist sites.

‌



More than 260,000 people have been evacuated from their homes in the Gironde region, where the main blaze began last Wednesday in a pine forest near the village of Saumos, about 25 miles west of Bordeaux.

‌



The latest evacuation order covers campsites, holiday villages, tourist residences and leisure parks around the resort of Lacanau, Gironde regional authorities said.

‌



The fires have ravaged the Cap Ferret peninsula and scorched 42,000 hectares - an area four times the size of Paris - but were kept under control overnight.

View 3 Images A map shows the active wildfires in France's Gironde region (Image: Datawrapper)

France wildfires live: Thousands of tourists evacuated from coast near Bordeaux READ MORE :

UK weather maps show 11 counties at 35C or more as 36C heatwave peaks in hours READ MORE :

Officials said on Tuesday morning that the main blaze has stabilised and the burned area remains unchanged, but warned it could still burn out of control again as temperatures rise and humidity falls.

‌



National weather service Météo-France said France’s latest heatwave is expected to begin today (Tuesday)

Much of the country is forecast to see highs of 32C to 35C, with temperatures reaching 37C in the south-west. Nantes and Paris are set to hit 33C, while Lyon could reach 34C and Toulouse 35C.

Temperatures are expected to climb still further on Wednesday, with intense heat spreading across much of western France. Parts of the south-west could see scorching highs of 40C, while Paris is forecast to reach 38C and Lyon 36C.

‌



View 3 Images A firefighter works to extinguish flames near Lacanau as wildfires rage outside Bordeaux, France (Image: AP Photo/Baz Ratner)

The weather service has placed Gironde under a yellow heat warning from midday on Tuesday.

"We’re facing a completely unprecedented fire," French President Emmanuel Macron said on Monday, describing the situation as France’s worst fire-related crisis since World War II.

Article continues below

More than 448 square miles have burned across France this year, according to the interior ministry.

Europe is the world’s fastest-warming continent, heating at more than twice the global average, according to the European Union's Copernicus climate service.

News.title: Love Island final LIVE: Jasmine answers speculation she was fuming over Julia's win
News.content:
Tonight's final of Love Island will crown the 13th season's winners as Priya responds to 'job-shaming' allegations after Elicia comment

The Love Island has officially ended with Lorenzo Alessi and Julia Majchrzak announced as winners, beating out stiff competition from Kavan Murphy and Jasmine Muller.

However, it wasn't without drama as one Islander was noticeably absent from the proceedings, while fans were convinced that there was drama brewing between others.

Over the last few weeks, fans have voiced their belief that there was a row between Julia and Jas - which ramped up during last night's episode, as eagle-eyed viewers suggested that the latter snubbed her co-star over the win.

Social media users pored over the specific moment Maya announced the winners, where it seemed as though the Islanders ignored each other and failed to hug during the celebrations.

Jas was quick to squash the claims in her Debrief interview, telling hosts Shakira, Toni and Yasmin: “It’s so funny because in here - you guys know - it feels like such a big deal and then the minute you’re hanging out, it’s so minor and everything is minor.

“She’s actually iconic as hell, so we’re good.”

Here's everything else that went down as the new champions were crowned...

News.title: Japan earthquake live: 'Many fatalities' as mall explodes during 7.1-mag quake
News.content:
Multiple people have died while more are missing after a shopping centre collapsed following a huge 7.1 magnitude earthquake on the Japanese island of Kyushu

Authorities in Japan say there are 'many fatalities' following the horror collapse of a major shopping centre during today's powerful earthquake.

Up to 30 others remain missing at the Aeon Mall in Kumamoto, while employees are also missing at the nearby Nippon Paper Industries Yatsushiro Plant.

The massive quake measured at the highest possible level seven on Japan's own Shindo "scale of shaking" and has left tens of thousands without power. Kumamoto Airport has been closed indefinitely after the earthquake rocked its runway.

A tsunami warning was issued after the 7.1 magnitude quake rocked multiple towns in Kumamoto province on the southern Japanese island of Kyushu - where roughly 13million people live. The alert was for the province's Ariake bay but has since been lifted.

Kumamoto was hit with a deadly quake in 2016 that left more than 50 people dead, 1,800 injured and tens of thousands of homes damaged or destroyed.

News.title: Evacuation in Amsterdam as car 'carrying explosives' crashes after Germany ram-raid
News.content:
Evacuation in Amsterdam as car 'carrying explosives' crashes after Germany ram-raid

The incident occurred in the Osdorp neighbourhood in Amsterdam in the Netherlands after a ram-raid in Germany, with emergency services on Nierkerkestraat

View 2 Images The police and the military are among the emergency services at the scene (Image: Getty Images)

A car 'containing explosives' has been involved in a crash in a neighbourhood in Amsterdam following a police chase.

‌



The incident happened this afternoon following a pursuit after an ATM ram-raid in Germany, according to local reports. The police, the military and other emergency services are on scene on Nierkerkestraat in Osdorp.

‌



The street is cordoned off and homes on a hundred-metre radius have been evacuated as possible explosives were found in the crashed vehicle. The car's occupants fled the scene and they remain at large.

‌



View 2 Images A police cordon is in place on Nierkerkestraat, as emergency services remain on scene (Image: Getty Images)

The police pursuit reportedly started after a ram-raid in Germany last night, which allegedly involved a BMW M1. The vehicle is understood to have been seen in the city of Fürth in Bavaria, central Germany, before it was spotted in the Netherlands this morning.

‌



The same car then crashed in Amsterdam Nieuw-West during the police chase, Dutch news website Nos reports. No money was stolen during the ATM explosion, German police explained, but the building in which the ATM was located was severely damaged.

A fire started as a result of the explosion but all residents were able to leave their homes safely. Armed forces personnel and masked officers from the Special Intervention Service remain at the scene in Fürth.

A police helicopter was also sent to circle overhead and the street where the explosion happened was cordoned off. A major incident was declared and videos from the scene showed multiple ambulances in the area.

News.title: Luxurious UK chocolate brand loved by royal family plunged into administration
News.content:
Luxurious UK chocolate brand loved by royal family plunged into administration

The historic chocolatier that inspired Roald Dahl and held two Royal Warrants closed its doors after facing significant challenges.

View 3 Images The chocolatier has closed its doors (Image: Octavian Lazar via Getty Images)

One of Britain's most famous chocolate institutions is in administration following 40 years in business. The closure of Prestat's historic Piccadilly shop marks the end of an era for a brand that once won over royalty, inspired a beloved children's author, and was hailed as one of the finest chocolate shops in the world.

‌



The shutters came down after Marasu's Petit Fours appointed administrators on February 6 — with the announcement made public on February 17.

‌



Founded in 1986 by patissiers Rolf Kern and Gabi Kohler, Marasu's Petit Fours had grown to become London's largest producer of premium chocolates, turning out over 300 tonnes per year from its 25,000 sq ft Park Royal facilities.

‌



View 3 Images The brand's chocolates inspired Roald Dahl (Image: Getty)

Why did Prestat's close down?

The chocolate industry has been battered in recent years by rising costs. Global cocoa prices surged to record highs in 2024, driven by crops devastated by disease and extreme weather, including flooding and droughts in key producing nations.

Ghana and the Ivory Coast together account for approximately 60% of the world's cocoa production, and their struggles had a domino effect across the sector.

‌



Marasu's reportedly compounded its difficulties by pushing into premium cocoa varieties such as Criollo in a bid to expand its market, leaving the company exposed to cheaper rivals at a time when it could least afford it.

The closure formed part of a prepack administration deal in which the Prestat brand has been sold for a nominal sum to L'Artisan du Chocolat, owned by Polus Capital Management.

The agreement was struck before administrators were formally appointed, and Prestat is expected to continue trading as an online-only brand.

‌



View 3 Images Marasu's is closing after 40 years in business (Image: Getty)

Prestat held two Royal Warrants and counted the Royal Family — including Princess Diana — among its most famous customers. In 2003, The Economist named it one of the top three chocolate shops in the world.

Most famously, the Piccadilly shop captured the imagination of Roald Dahl, who referenced Prestat's truffles in his novel My Uncle Oswald, and is widely said to have inspired the fantastical sweet shop at the heart of Charlie and the Chocolate Factory. The store was also one of the few remaining chocolatiers to craft its own chocolates on the premises — a tradition that will now come to an end.

Article continues below

Can you still buy Prestat's chocolates?

Even though the iconic store has closed down, you can still shop online for Prestat chocolate. The Prestat website itself is still active, and certain products are also stocked on the likes of Ocado and Selfridges too.

Prestat also regularly shares updates on Instagram, featuring news of new releases, gifts and more.

News.title: Powell says student loan system at top of in-tray
News.content:
Lucy Powell has said she wants to make sure the student loans system is "fair" and that the issue is at the top of her in-tray as the new education secretary.

Labour's deputy leader told the BBC she stood by comments she made in February that the interest rates graduates with Plan 2 loans were paying were "egregious".

She said she was committed to looking at the issue, although acknowledged she "can't make any promises" about changes.

Plan 2 loans were taken out by students in England between September 2012 and July 2023, and are still issued in Wales. Graduates pay back what they earn above the repayment threshold at a rate of 9%.

In November last year, then-Chancellor Rachel Reeves said the repayment threshold for students with Plan 2 loans would be frozen at Â£29,385 between 2027 and 2030, instead of rising with inflation.

The change would result in students starting to repay their loans sooner than they would otherwise have done, and their rising salaries leading to greater repayments.

Campaigners have called for that decision to be reversed.

Reeves later said the government's measures were "fair and proportionate" for getting "the balance right between tax and spending".

In April, the government said interest on some student loans in England - including Plan 2 - would be capped at 6%.

Speaking to Matt Chorley on BBC Radio 5 Live, Powell said she was "very familiar" with the issue as her eldest child has a Plan 2 loan.

She said: "I think it's not just about the threshold of when people start to pay it back, but also the interest rate which is RPI [retail prices index] plus 3%.

"I think I've called it in the past egregious and I'm not going to change my opinion on that just because I'm now the secretary of state.

"The government has committed to a review of that, it's very much at the top of my in-tray as the secretary of state, and I want to make sure we look at this so it's fair for students."

Powell described it as a "real cost-of-living issue" for young people, adding: "They're paying high repayments and never, ever paying off the capital of their student loan."

Pressed on whether it is something she will look at, Powell replied: "Yes. I can't make any promises, but it needs looking at."

MPs on the Treasury Committee this month said comparing student loan repayments to phone contracts or cinema tickets "amounted to mis-selling" by government.

It came after a BBC investigation found the government compared student loan repayments to Â£30-a-month phone contracts in promotional presentations to teenagers a decade ago.

Earlier this year, Conservative leader Kemi Badenoch said she would cut the rate of interest charged on Plan 2 loans, capping it at RPI only. The current RPI rate is 3%.

News.title: Naga Munchetty to leave BBC Breakfast after 17 years
News.content:
Munchetty, 51, is among the best-paid presenters on the BBC's star salaries list, earning about Â£360,000 a year, according to the latest accounts.

She has interviewed major celebrities and politicians on the programme over the years ranging from Hillary Clinton and Michelle Obama to Sir Keir Starmer, Sir David Attenborough and Sir Rod Stewart.

In 2016, she appeared on the BBC's Strictly Come Dancing.

She has also been at the centre of some controversies during her time on BBC Breakfast.

In 2019, she was initially found to have breached the BBC's guidelines over comments she made about a social media post from Donald Trump about four female politicians of colour.

However, the BBC's director general then reversed that finding after deciding her words were not "sufficient to merit" upholding part of the complaint.

In 2021, Munchetty and co-presenter Charlie Stayt were "spoken to and reminded of their responsibilities" after complaints about their reaction to a government minister's flag. Munchetty apologised for liking "offensive" tweets about the exchange.

In June 2025, the Sun reported details of two alleged incidents which the paper said caused BBC bosses to speak to Munchetty about her conduct.

That came amid reports of behind-the-scenes tensions on the show, and at the same time as the programme's editor Richard Frediani took extended leave following allegations about his behaviour.

The BBC said it did not comment on individual cases but took all complaints about conduct at work extremely seriously.

Munchetty and Frediani did not comment on the reports.

News.title: Schools to offer technical subjects from age 14 in England, Burnham says
News.content:
Secondary school pupils in England will be able to study subjects like manufacturing and AI in addition to core academic learning under reforms outlined by Prime Minister Andy Burnham.

The government said the courses, which would be available from Year 10, would be linked to local industries and designed to give children a clearer pathway into work.

Data published this year showed more than one million young people across the UK were not in education, employment or training, the highest level in more than 12 years.

Few details have been published about how the new vocational courses would work in practice and it is not clear how they would operate in areas with low industrial activity.

The BBC understands that the government expects the new pathways into work to be up and running in some areas by 2028.

Speaking at a train manufacturing site in Derby, Burnham said: "We've had a system built for too long around the university route and it sends a message to some young people that they're some kind of second-class citizens, and it's just not right.

"They need an education system that works for them as well, that offers a path to all young people, that's balanced between academic and technical."

The prime minister said he was "on a mission" to reduce the number of young people not in education, employment or training - known as "Neet" - but declined to put a target date on his ambition.

"The trend is rising at the moment, so the first thing I've got to do is to stop that rise," he said.

"It's hard to put a firm date on the moment when you can say there are fewer than now."

However, shadow work and pensions secretary Helen Whately said while there was a "broad consensus" on improving vocational education, it was "not a big bold announcement".

She told BBC Breakfast: "What's going on there is a drastic shortage of jobs because Labour's policies over the last couple of years have killed job opportunities for young people. This announcement will not solve that."

News.title: Odyssey translator writes scathing review of Nolan film adaptation
News.content:
Sir Christopher Nolan's latest film, The Odyssey, may have won rave reviews from critics and done storming business at the box office - but one person is definitely not happy.

Emily Wilson, the academic whose 2017 translation of Homer's Odyssey was cited by the director as an influence on his adaptation of the poem, has written a scathing review of the movie.

Published in the London Review of Books, external, Wilson said she "would be ashamed to have written any of this script", describing the film's narrative structure as "gimmicky."

"The writing is abysmal," she said. "None of the characters has convincing motivation for their actions or words. There are no sex scenes, and all the food looks horrible."

News.title: Mother and boyfriend guilty of murder of girl, two
News.content:
Warning: This story contains distressing details

A mother and her new boyfriend have been found guilty of murdering her two-year-old daughter, with the man also convicted of sexually abusing the girl.

Isabelle Welsh suffered multiple injuries in the weeks before she collapsed with a fractured skull at her home in Thornaby in September 2025, Teesside Crown Court had heard.

Alexandra Walker, 25, and her partner Harrison Simpson, 22, were both found guilty of murder and child cruelty, with Simpson also convicted of sexual abuse of a child.

They will be sentenced on Thursday. Isabelle's family said she had her "whole life ahead of her" but it was "taken in the most heartbreaking way".

Prosecutors previously said the couple, who began a relationship in June 2025, were both responsible for a "wicked" campaign of sexual abuse and violence against Isabelle.

Walker and Simpson blamed each other for the girl's injuries and suffering.

News.title: House of the Dragon star Bethany Antonia joins Strictly line-up
News.content:
House of the Dragon star Bethany Antonia is the latest celebrity to join this year's line-up for Strictly Come Dancing.

Antonia has portrayed dragon-rider Lady Baela Targaryen in HBO's Game of Thrones prequel since 2022. She is currently starring as Eurydice in the Tony Award-winning musical Hadestown in London's West End.

The singer and actress has also appeared in series including Nolly, Stay Close, Stath Lets Flats, and Doctor Who.

In a statement, Antonia said: "I can't quite believe that I will be heading to the Strictly ballroom this September! I have grown up watching Strictly, and I am so excited to take the challenge on and (hopefully!) learn a new skill. See you on the dancefloor!"

She is the ninth celebrity to be confirmed for this year's series, joining stars including Delta Goodrem, Lacey Turner, Dani Dyer and Jaime Winstone.

More celebrities are set to be announced in the coming weeks, with 15 expected in the final line-up.

News.title: 'It's a hell of a situation': Spain grapples with destructive wildfires
News.content:
Temperatures are expected to approach 40C in some regions in the coming days, with the heatwave forecast to last at least until Sunday.

Spain's state meteorological agency Aemet has warned the "fire danger level will continue to rise to extreme levels, hindering firefighting efforts".

Regional authorities began lifting some evacuation and lockdown orders on Tuesday as conditions improved - including in parts of the Madrid region - but restrictions remain in place in the worst-affected areas.

In the Madrid region alone, more than 56,500 people have been evacuated since the fires broke out last week. A further 27,797 people have been ordered to stay at home.

Further evacuations have taken place in Ãvila, Toledo and Valencia.

Ayuso had earlier described the wildfires as "the biggest natural catastrophe in the history of Spain".

She wrote on X that the situation was now "improving little by little" and some residents may soon be allowed to return home.

Interior Minister Fernando Grande-Marlaska told Spain's La 1 TV channel that firefighting efforts on Monday night had resulted in "relatively positive progress".

"This morning, we are very satisfied with the work done. We are going to consolidate the work that has been done," he said.

He maintained that "we must be positive; we have the emergency under control" but conceded that "weather conditions are not helping us at all".

News.title: Is it safe to travel to Spain and France right now?
News.content:
The UK government has not specifically warned against travel to anywhere in France or Spain, but it does advise caution.

In France, it says access to affected areas may be restricted and roads may close at short notice. It adds that further evacuations may take place.

It has also issued a general warning about the high risk of wildfires in France during the summer season from April to October.

For those in an affected area in France or Spain or planning to travel there, the UK government recommends following instructions and updates from local authorities and emergency services at all times.

Those needing emergency help in France or Spain can call 112.

Travellers should also bear in mind the UK government's advice can and does change in response to moving events.

Anna-Marie Duthie, travel insurance expert at financial rating firm Defaqto, says that if this happens after you have booked your trip, "you may be covered for cancellation or curtailment".

"You may also be covered for additional travel and accommodation costs should your trip be disrupted due to a catastrophic event, if your insurer offers this cover or you've paid to include it," she adds.

To know if this applies to you, check your policy.

News.title: Fourth heatwave grips parts of UK with 35C forecast
News.content:
A fourth heatwave of the year is now under way for parts of the UK, with temperatures expected to climb into the mid-30s Celsius later this week.

This latest spell of heatwave threshold-level temperatures is expected to peak on Wednesday in the south-east and east of England.

The UK Health Security Agency (UKHSA) has warned the rising temperatures could increase health risks, particularly for vulnerable groups.

It has issued amber heat health alerts, external for much of eastern England that come into force on Wednesday.

News.title: Unsolved Suzy Lamplugh case 'haunts' detectives
News.content:
Police officers investigating the disappearance of estate agent Suzy Lamplugh in west London say they remain "haunted" by the case, four decades after she went missing.

Lamplugh, 25, vanished after leaving her Fulham office to meet a client on the afternoon of 28 July 1986. She never returned and her body has never been found.

As the Metropolitan Police investigation is due to be mothballed next year, cold case detectives say they are troubled by the continuing mystery.

To mark the 40th anniversary of her disappearance, the Lamplugh family has released previously unseen photographs featuring her siblings Lizzie, Tamsin and Richard and her parents Paul and Diana.

In releasing the intimate family images, her siblings described her as "a truly beautiful person inside and out".

News.title: Hundreds of thousands of women get morning-after pill via free pharmacy service
News.content:
The morning-after pill, known as emergency contraception, external, is medication designed to prevent unwanted pregnancies. It usually has to be taken within three to five days of having unprotected sex. The sooner it is taken, the more effective it is.

It works by delaying or preventing the release of an egg, but will only prevent pregnancy if ovulation has not already happened.

Alternatively, women can visit a doctor or nurse to have a coil or intrauterine device (IUD) fitted to prevent pregnancy at any time during their menstrual cycle. To be effective, it needs to be fitted within 120 hours or five days of unprotected sex.

The government said making the morning-after pill available free from pharmacies would end the "unfair" barriers and postcode lottery some women faced - with access varying dramatically depending on where they live.

Under the scheme, women can visit their local pharmacy and have a confidential consultation with a pharmacist or trained pharmacy technician, before receiving the medication on the same day.

Prior to this, women had to book an appointment with their GP, sexual health clinic or pharmacy to get the morning-after pill. Women could also access it privately, as they still can now.

In 2024/25, there were around 150,000 NHS prescriptions for the morning-after pill - far fewer than under the new service.

Dr Sue Mann, NHS National Clinical Director for Women's Health, said the pharmacy service was a "major step forward for women's health", with "no appointment, no waiting and no judgement".

"This service is already making a real impact, particularly for women living in more deprived communities, by making contraception easier to access closer to home," she added.

Women can check online, external to find their nearest participating pharmacy. All pharmacists and pharmacy technicians delivering the service have received specialist training to provide emergency contraception and wider contraceptive care.

News.title: Man guilty of murdering two men found in woods
News.content:
A man has been found guilty of murdering two men he met in a homeless shelter.

James Desborough had previously admitted preventing the lawful burial in 2025 of 57-year-old Claudio Aquilino and 43-year-old Daniel Coleman.

A jury at Winchester Crown Court heard the 40-year-old, of Old Oak Woods, Lower Sticker, Cornwall, dismembered the victims' bodies, tried to burn their remains and hide them in woodland where he owns a cabin.

In March, Desborough was found guilty of murdering his cellmate at Exeter Prison while on remand for this trial. He was sentenced to 19 years in prison for that charge.

News.title: Richard Hammond fined £999 for  speeding offences
News.content:
Former Top Gear presenter Richard Hammond has been fined Â£999 after being caught speeding twice in three weeks while driving luxury cars.

The 56-year-old was captured driving his Porsche Taycan Cross Turismo at 68mph in a 50mph limit on the A40 in Pencraig, Herefordshire on 2 December.

He was later clocked driving his Bentley Continental GT at 82mph in a 70mph limit on the A50 Rudhall Overbridge, also in Herefordshire, on 22 December.

Hammond pleaded guilty to two speeding charges through his solicitor. Two further charges that he had ignored the police letters and failed to identify himself as the guilty driver were withdrawn by police.

He was also given seven penalty points for his licence at the hearing last week.

Magistrate Ann Minton ordered him to pay a total of Â£1,771, comprising two fines of Â£333 and Â£666, Â£240 in costs and victim surcharges totalling Â£532.

News.title: The 10 most overcrowded commuter trains revealed
News.content:
The most overcrowded train service in England and Wales last autumn was a Thameslink morning rush hour service between Bedford and Three Bridges in West Sussex, according to the Department for Transport (DfT).

Second on the list was a West Midlands service from London Euston to Crewe, Cheshire, departing at 17:46, the government figures reveal.

Overall, they show overcrowding on commuter trains serving major English and Welsh cities fell slightly, for the first time since 2020, due to an increase in capacity.

Only 1.1% of peak-time travellers were on an overcrowded train, the DfT said. More than 1.2 million of the average 1.9 million journeys on a typical autumn day were in London.

The DfT says work is under way to improve capacity where there are pinch points during peak hours.

The Thameslink service which topped the list had a "load factor" â meaning how full the train was â of 176% at London St Pancras shortly after 08:00.

The West Midlands service to Crewe had a load factor of 170%. It was busiest when it departed Euston.

The third most crowded train was a Transport for Wales service from Bridgend to Rhymney, with a load factor of 161%. It was busiest at Llanishen.

Four of the top ten services were operated by South Western, and Thameslink appeared twice more.

Julia Majchrzak and Lorenzo Alessi have been crowned the winners of Love Island UK 2026.

The pair beat runners-up Jasmine Muller and Kavan Murphy, and Angelista Gunda and Simba Kudyiwa, who came in third, to take home the Â£50,000 prize.

A shocked Julia thanked all those who had voted for them, saying: "I just didn't think coming into Casa [Amor] I'd be stood here."

Talking to Maya ahead of the reveal during the live final, 28-year-old Lorenzo said he had "never met someone who feels so well matched to me" when reflecting on his relationship with Julia.

Business owner Lorenzo, who entered the villa on day one, said he felt like he "manifested" meeting Julia, 26, in Casa Amor, the alternate villa where relationships are tested by new arrivals.

California Gov. Gavin Newsom has trolled President Donald Trump over his decade-long promise to usher in a new healthcare plan, which is yet to come to fruition.

In January 2026, Trump announced that he was calling on Congress to enact the “Great Healthcare Plan” to lower drug prices and insurance premiums in a bid to hold insurance companies accountable.

But it appears to have fallen by the wayside amid the president’s war in Iran, his Washington, D.C. beautification project and other priorities.

The president once again renewed his pledge that the administration would pass the plan during his Monday speech in Michigan. But Newsom’s press office account on X pointed out that Trump has been promising to do this for years — and shared a link to a now-defunct webpage as proof.

“Trump’s made this promise FOR 9 YEARS, but you wouldn’t know that since the page with the transcript has seemingly been removed!” the Democrat’s team quipped.

open image in gallery California Gov. Gavin Newsom has trolled President Donald Trump over his decade-long promise to usher in a new healthcare plan, which is yet to come to fruition ( AFP via Getty Images )

The link to the White House website was for Trump’s 2017 Executive Order titled, “Promoting Healthcare Choice and Competition Across the United States,” which is no longer active.

“In the time President Trump secured multiple Most-Favored-Nation deals to lower prescription drug prices, Gavin successfully laid exactly zero miles of new high-speed rail track.” White House Spokesman Kush Desai said in a statement.

“We will pass the great healthcare plan. That's what it's called, the Great Healthcare plan, to stop all payments to big insurance companies and give the money directly to you, the people, so that they can buy their own healthcare,” Trump said during his Monday night speech in Michigan. “Which will be much less expensive and be a much better healthcare.”

Even before Trump’s first term, when he was on the presidential campaign trail in 2015 and 2016, it became a running joke that his healthcare plan was being rolled out “within two weeks” after he repeatedly made the promise that never materialized.

Critics said his recent healthcare pledge was reminiscent of that time, responding in droves to a clip of Monday’s speech.

“It's coming in two weeks!” said MeidasTouch editor Ron Filipkowski, while another said, “How many times has he said that? MAGA morons still think he’ll do it.”

open image in gallery Newsom’s press office account on X pointed out that Trump has been promising to bring in a new healthcare plan for years — and shared a link to a now-defunct webpage as proof ( @GovPressOffice )

“He promised this at the end of his first term, within two weeks,” another social media user noted.

“He promised this in 2016. It's 10 years later,” wrote another.

His long-awaited healthcare plan was unveiled in January by the White House. It would implement and fund a new cost-sharing plan aimed at driving down premiums for plans on the Affordable Care Act exchanges while also providing direct payments to Americans.

Likely to be put into legislation in the form of health savings accounts, the president’s direct payments would be a substitute for the direct federal subsidies for Obamacare plans in the form of premium tax credits passed in 2022. Those tax credits affected the vast majority of plans on the exchanges.

At the time, White House press secretary Karoline Leavitt claimed that the plan was “the most comprehensive and bold agenda to lower healthcare costs to have ever been considered.”

News.title: Dexter fan guilty of double murder after two men found dismembered in Cornish woods
News.content:

A fan of TV serial killer Dexter has been found guilty of murdering two homeless men whose bodies were dismembered and hidden in woodland before he killed his cellmate while awaiting trial.

James Desborough, 40, murdered Claudio Aquilino, 57, and Daniel Coleman, 43, before dismembering and hiding their bodies in Cornwall last year.

The former builder is already serving a life sentence after he strangled his prison cellmate Steven Kempster at HMP Exeter while on remand awaiting this trial.

The triple murderer is now a serial killer having killed three men in separate incidents over five months.

A jury at Winchester Crown Court returned the unanimous guilty verdicts on Tuesday after deliberating for three hours and 15 minutes.

Desborough showed no emotion as the verdicts were read out.

The trial heard Mr Aquilino and Mr Coleman had previously lived with Desborough at a homeless hostel, and the last time they were both seen alive was in his company.

After their disappearances, the powerfully-built Desborough, who is 5ft 10in and weighs nearly 18st, went on to spend their money on drugs and alcohol.

Their bodies were dismembered in an area of Sticker Woods, near St Austell, where Desborough lived in a wooden cabin.

It was there that police discovered deposited in a stream 1,900 burned bone fragments from the body of Mr Aquilino.

Parts of Mr Coleman’s body, including his torso, legs and feet, were found in a shallow grave nearby.

Desborough told a forensic biologist who was searching the woods for Mr Coleman’s body that he “particularly enjoyed the dismemberment scenes” in the television series Dexter.

Police found several handwritten notes inside Desborough’s cabin, including one headed: “Bug out list” and another: “Hostiles”.

Among the notes were one which said: “I know I am a killer and ready to execute any predators” and another that said: “Take care of the remaining muppets,” with Mr Coleman’s name also listed.

Desborough also drew a series of concentric circles with Sticker Woods in the centre, and London and Benidorm listed at the outer point, which was entitled: “Kill Zone”, and the sub-heading: “Operational spheres”.

He had also made plans to the leave the UK weeks before he was arrested.

The father-of-one denied both murders and told the jury it was a “series of unfortunate circumstances” the two men died on his land within a short space of time.

Desborough killed Mr Aquilino, who had addictions to drugs and gambling, shortly after he was last seen alive in April last year.

The defendant maintained he had in fact while high on ketamine found Mr Aquilino, who had a history of suicidal ideation, hanging dead from a tree on his land in May or early June.

And his role was helping Mr Coleman – who had dismembered and burnt the remains alone – dispose of Mr Aquilino’s body in a stream, Desborough said.

He said Mr Coleman calmed him down and convinced him to dispose of the body and carry on using Mr Aquilino’s bank card.

“The idea was to cover up the death, carry on using his card. I’m not proud of it, it was like dangling the carrot,” he said.

“I was homeless, jobless, I had no money and addiction problems.”

He also denied murdering Mr Coleman in the early hours of June 4, and instead insisted he had returned to his cabin later that month and found him lying naked, face down and dead in a stream.

Worried about there already being one dead body on his land and that he was in possession of Class A drugs, he dismembered Mr Coleman using an axe and buried the remains.

He accepted then spending their money on beer and drugs, but told jurors: “They were friends, I got on well with them.”

Desborough, of Old Oak Woods, Lower Sticker, Cornwall, had previously pleaded guilty to preventing the lawful burial of the two men’s bodies.
