Kemi Badenoch has urged the public to support prison-building in their area amid a row over Labour’s plan to release some criminals early.

Just days after Andy Burnham announced plans to pause its early release scheme, the Conservative leader appealed to voters, saying: “If everybody says ‘no prison near me’, we won’t get these built”.

She also said the prime minister should go further than simply pausing the plans, instead calling for him to change the law.

Under changes in the Sentencing Act, some 6,000 offenders were expected to be freed from prison in September after serving a third of their sentence – rather than half – in a bid to ease prison overcrowding.

open image in gallery Conservative Party leader Kemi Badenoch said Zack Polanski and Nigel Farage are ‘spending too much time on Twitter and Instagram’ (Jonathan Brady/PA) ( PA Wire )

At a press conference on Tuesday, Mrs Badenoch said: “We do need to build new prison places more quickly and cheaply. This will cost money but it also needs communities to be supportive of prisons being built around them.

“One of the things that did cause delays was judicial reviews of prisons not being built.

“If everybody says ‘no prison near me’, we won’t get these built, so this is something that the public can help with – let us build prisons to put these people in. We cannot say ‘no’ to every potential site for a prison.”

She also called for the Labour government to rent prison places overseas and to remove foreign offenders to their home countries.

“The second thing that we can do a little bit earlier is rent prison places overseas. This was something which we were doing in government, we had plans to rent prison places just like Sweden has done with Estonia so that we didn’t have to just release these sorts of violent criminals early”, Mrs Badenoch said.

Calling for the government to “remove foreign offenders to prisons in their home countries”, she said the UK must “leave the (European) Convention on Human Rights”, which she described as a blocker on removals.

Claiming Mr Burnham “hasn’t done anything at all to pause” the early release programme, Ms Badenoch said: “If Andy Burnham wants to prove that he is serious about this, he needs to revoke the commencement order... That would show that he is really pausing it. And then he needs to bring in emergency legislation by September 2.”

Mr Burnham said he would do “anything I can to minimise the risk to the public” but blamed the Tories for failing to build enough prison places to prevent overcrowding.

The prime minister told reporters: “It is a challenging situation, and we shouldn’t actually be in this position as a country. But we have to deal with the reality of where we are.”

open image in gallery Andy Burnham has paused Labour’s early release scheme ( PA Wire )

He added: “The pause is real and it was one of the first things I did coming into office last week, so the September releases is on hold.

“And then secondly, the review that I have instigated is also a real process and we are taking a very serious look at the situation.

“Of course, this goes back a number of years when the previous government failed to put in place the prison places needed.”

Reforms in the Sentencing Act came after prisons came close to running out of space entirely last year, risking the “total breakdown of law and order”, which would leave police unable to make arrests and courts unable to send offenders to custody, the then justice secretary Shabana Mahmood said.

Mrs Badenoch admitted that “the situation with prisons is challenging” but said her party “never had killers, rapists, paedophiles on early release”.

“When we were in government, we saw the challenge. We created 14,000 prison new prison places, it was nowhere near enough”, she said.

“We had a prison-building target in our manifesto. Covid derailed that programme.”

Last week, Mr Burnhamvowed that “no prisoners will be let out under this policy” pending an “urgent review” following a row over the policy which broke out after it was revealed that two of those responsible for the death of PC Harper could be eligible for automatic release under the scheme.

The police officer was 28 when he sustained fatal injuries after getting his feet caught in a strap attached to the back of a car and dragged for a mile as three teenage suspects fled the scene of a burglary in Berkshire in 2019.

Lissie Harper, PC Harper’s widow, described the scheme as “deplorable” and accused politicians of “making decisions from behind a desk that will have real and lasting consequences” for the families of victims.

A fourth live-action Paddington film is in development with A-list talent, Canal+ CEO Maxime Saada confirmed on Tuesday, adding fresh momentum to one of StudioCanal's biggest international franchises.

The pay-TV provider will also be the first to bring Paddington 4 to French small screens, just six months after its theatrical release. This follows their renewed agreement with French cinema organisations until 2032, committing investments for early access to new releases.

The group did not disclose the film's release date or distribution plans. Canal+ will invest about €1 billion ($1.2 billion) in French and European ​cinema ⁠over five years starting ‌from 2028. In return, it is granted privileged access to new theatrical releases under France's media laws, both for ‌its own films and acquired content — an ‌advantage as global streaming services compete for subscribers.

open image in gallery The previous Paddington movies were released in 2014, 2017 and 2024 and proved to be a huge success at the box office. ( PA )

"When we buy and we have deals with Universal, Warner, Paramount ... all of these ⁠movies are available on the Canal+ platform in France six months after release. When Netflix has a deal with Universal, they have to wait until 15 months to broadcast the movie (in France)," Saada told Reuters.

To secure the right to early releases, Canal+ is required to invest about €140 million a year, Saada said. "So we committed to spending an extra €50 million a year, approximately." The investment is ‌only one part of ⁠the group's much larger content budget. Canal+ spent €2.25 billion ⁠in content costs in the first half of 2026 alone, across films, ‌television and ​sport in its international markets. France generated €1.77 ‌billion of its first-half revenue, ​making it Canal+'s biggest individual market.

Earlier this year, Actor Hugh Bonneville indicated he is unlikely to return to the Paddington film franchise.

The 62-year-old, who plays Mr Brown in the children’s films, suggested the series would continue without him as its focus remains on the bear.

Asked about a potential return to Paddington, he told Saga Magazine: "I don’t think so. I really don’t. I’ve loved it, but I’m getting on a bit. It’s a younger man’s job, but you can get other actors in and it will work just as well, because it’s all about the bear."

Armando Iannucci, the Oscar-nominated screenwriter behind the sweary, satirical classic The Thick Of It, has also been revealed as the writer for Paddington 4.

open image in gallery Actor Hugh Bonneville has revealed he will not return to the Paddington film franchise. ( PA Wire )

The Scottish writer – who also penned Veep, The Death of Stalin and the admittedly more niche 2006 series Time Trumpet – has reportedly joined as one half of the writing team who will mastermind the Peruvian bear’s next adventure.

According to Variety, Iannucci will reunite with frequent collaborator Simon Blackwell for the project, which was announced at ComicCon earlier this year.

Paddington, first published on October 13 1958, has seen a number of adaptations over the years, including a BBC TV version in 1976, voiced by the late Sir Michael Hordern.

The movies, featuring Ben Whishaw as the voice of Paddington, produced by StudioCanal, were released in 2014, 2017 and 2024 and proved to be a huge success at the box office.

Paddington The Musical is currently playing in London’s West End at the Savoy Theatre.

The stage show features original music by McFly’s Tom Fletcher. "It’s an honour to be entrusted to bring the story of Paddington to life on stage with the very best of creative collaborators in (playwright) Jessica (Swale), (theatre director) Luke (Sheppard), and our producers Sonia (Friedman) and Eliza (Lumley),” Fletcher said.

Reform UK has reported Green Party leader Zack Polanski to the police and accused him of “inciting murder” after a picture was shared on social media.

The image, which was subsequently unshared from Mr Polanski’s Instagram account, featured a man wearing a black T-shirt with the message “We’re only making plans for Nigel” and an image of a guillotine.

Sharing a screenshot of the image, Reform UK leader Nigel Farage wrote on social media: “This is what Zack Polanski has just posted on his Instagram.

“If I was to post anything as inciteful then I would expect to be arrested, and so should Polanski.”

‘Making Plans For Nigel’ is a song by English rock band XTC, released as the lead single from their 1979 album Drums And Wires.

open image in gallery Green Party leader Zack Polanski later unshared the image ( PA Wire )

A post on a website appearing to sell the T-shirt for £20 stated: “Who could Nigel be? And why the guillotine?

“Whether it’s a nod to old punk music or a sharper bit of political satire, this design is for those who prefer their statements with a side of mystery.”

The Green Party said Mr Polanski “condemns the image on the T-shirt” and clicked accept to be tagged in a post with 20 images “without realising there was more to it than he had seen”.

But Reform’s home affairs spokesperson Zia Yusuf claimed the Green Party leader was “inciting murder”, adding that sharing the image weeks after the death of Ann Widdecombe was “staggering”.

Prosecutors told a court last week that a man allegedly hit the Reform UK spokesperson and former Tory minister 21 times over the head with a hammer in a “planned and targeted” attack.

A spokesperson for the Metropolitan Police said: “Earlier today – Monday, 27 July – we received a third-party report relating to an image shared on social media.

“We take reports of this nature extremely seriously, and officers are conducting inquiries into the matter.”

Reform UK’s spokesperson for home affairs Mr Yusuf wrote on social media: “Zack Polanski has posted to his 713k Instagram followers a photo of a man in a T-shirt calling for the beheading of Nigel Farage.

“Polanski is inciting murder. It must be treated as such by the police.”

open image in gallery Reform UK leader Nigel Farage condemned the post on social media ( PA Wire )

A Green Party spokesperson said: “Zack condemns the image on the T-shirt. He was tagged in a post with 20 images and clicked accept without realising there was more to it than he had seen.

“The T-shirt is clearly in poor taste, especially at a time of heightened fears for the security of public figures having experienced multiple threats himself.

“He and the Green Party call on everyone involved in public discourse to show kindness and not encourage more division.”

Prime minister Andy Burnham has said a “serious review” into MPs’ security is needed following the death of Ms Widdecombe, saying politics has “darkened” in the near decade since he was last in Westminster and protections may need to be “increased further.”

Mr Burnham, who previously served as MP for Leigh until 2017, said: “It’s obviously appalling what happened to Ann. I knew Ann over many years in the House, and you know, we would get along – and everybody would get along.

“But it feels as though something has changed. It’s easy to blame social media, but it feels like it’s having some impact in just building that kind of toxicity that’s around the political debate.”

He said the issue could not be solved by “easy, glib answers,” adding: “I do think we need now a serious review of MPs’ security.

“I certainly am prepared to do that.”

News.title: Dramatic rescue sees lifeguards battle terrifying waves to save boy off California
News.content:
A child was saved from the ocean in a dramatic rescue after being pulled in by powerful waves.

Footage captured by witness Scott Vander Dussem shows a Santa Cruz lifeguard, who is reportedly 16-years-old, pulling the boy from under the relentless surf on Saturday (25 July).

“It [the waves] caught a lot of people off-guard,” Mr Vander Dussen told NBC Bay Area. “Unfortunately, this young man was overwhelmed and swept out in just a moment’s time.”

A second lifeguard and beachgoers then rushed out to save the boy, who paramedics later evaluated before being released to his parents.

It was one of at least 25 rescues reported Saturday in Santa Cruz County, as huge swells battered the shoreline.

Roughly 40 percent of Americans are eating or buying less fresh fruit and vegetables due to nationwide outbreaks of a foodborne illness that leaves victims with explosive diarrhea, a new survey has found.

Cyclosporiasis has sickened 16,000 people across over 40 states with Michigan experiencing more than 9,200 cases. At least 300 people have been hospitalized but no deaths have been reported.

Infections are caused by the parasite cyclospora, with exposure leading to explosive diarrhea, fever, fatigue and dehydration.

The source of multiple outbreaks remains under investigation but some cases have been linked to contaminated iceberg lettuce, parsley and cilantro, federal and state health officials say.

A CBS News survey of more than 2,000 adults last week found that more than half of Americans haven’t changed their eating or buying habits - even as 43 percent of Americans said they were following the outbreak “somewhat closely.”

open image in gallery Cyclosporiasis has sickened 16,000 people across over 40 states and several outbreaks have been linked to fresh produce. A new poll found Americans are skipping buying fruits and vegetables because of the outbreak ( Getty )

The best way to avoid getting sick is to stop eating potentially-contaminated foods, or cook produce at a temperature of 158 degrees Fahrenheit that kills the parasite.

However, experts warn that avoiding produce isn’t the answer as it can come with further consequences for our health. Fruits and vegetables are packed with vitamins and essential minerals that the body needs to stay healthy. Yet, most Americans aren’t getting enough already.

Not getting enough fruits and vegetables can lead to weight gain that raises the risk of life-threatening heart disease, contribute to poor gut health that increases the likelihood of developing cancer and increase the likelihood of premature death.

“About 90 percent of Americans already eat too few vegetables, and 80 percent eat too little fruit,” emergency physician Dr. Leana Wen wrote in an op-ed in The Washington Post last week. “The last thing they need is for sensational headlines to make it even harder for them to choose fresh produce.”

People should throw out produce when it’s linked to outbreaks, but not avoid fruits and vegetables altogether, she urged.

Another way for Americans to better protect themselves going forward is to stay informed.

“Rather than avoiding all fresh produce, consumers should stay informed about outbreak announcements, pay attention to recalls and public health advisories, wash produce under running water and continue eating a healthy diet,” food safety and consumer policy expert Darin Detwiler, a professor emeritus at Northeastern University, told Serious Eats.

“The nutritional benefits of fruits and vegetables far outweigh the relatively small risk posed by any single outbreak,” he said.

open image in gallery Washing produce is an important step to reduce the risk for cyclosporiasis ( Getty )

While washing fruit and vegetables with care doesn’t eliminate cyclospora, it remains an important step to reduce risk – especially with produce that may not be smooth-skinned.

“Some people mistakenly conclude that because washing cannot remove every parasite, washing doesn’t matter,” Detwiler said.

Washing your hands is also an important step. The parasite spreads through traces of human waste.

Although in outbreaks as big as the current one, it’s believed that contaminated water on crops may be responsible.

“You’d have to have a lot of produce being irrigated with a lot of water that was contaminated by a lot of cyclospora to see this number of cases,” Keith Schneider, a professor of food safety at the University of Florida, told The New York Times last week.

News.title: Explosive mpox outbreak causes 3,000 cases in Madagascar
News.content:
More than 3,000 cases of mpox have been recorded in Madagascar after the virus spread from a single port city to some of the country’s busiest coastal hubs.

A total of 3,022 cases and 20 deaths have been recorded as of this week, with cases in Toamasina and Taolagnaro accounting for more than half of all diagnoses.

The outbreak has been linked to Clade 1b mpox, a strain that emerged in the Democratic Republic of the Congo in 2024, prompting the World Health Organization (WHO) to declare a global public health emergency at the time.

“The main factor driving the continued spread of the disease is human mobility, seeding new outbreaks in areas where the virus has not circulated before,” Professor Carlos Maluquer de Motes of the University of Surrey told The Telegraph.

“Under-reporting is likely, with the real number of cases exceeding what is being reported.”

News.title: Chelsea in 10-goal thriller as ‘Alonso ball’ brings risk and reward
News.content:
Chelsea’s first match under the management of Xabi Alonso was a 10-goal thriller in Australia, as the Premier League side eventually showed their class in a 6-4 win over Western Sydney Wanderers.

Star striker João Pedro, who was controversially left out of Brazil’s World Cup squad, scored a nine-minute hat-trick after coming off the bench with half an hour of the friendly remaining.

Alonso had selected a youthful team for the first hour before bringing nine senior players, including João Pedro, into the side in the second half. According to Transfermarkt, Chelsea’s squad is valued at over £1.3bn while their opponents a more modest £5.86m.

Teenage signing Dastan Satpayev, midfielder Dario Essugo and winger Jamie Gittens also found the net for Chelsea, who were defensively vulnerable for long spells for the game.

Here are five things Telegraph Sport learned from Alonso’s first match.

João Pedro picks up where he left off

João Pedro scored 13 goals in the second half of last season and his impressive performances resulted in the 24-year-old being named Chelsea’s player of the campaign. It was something of a surprise, then, when he was left out of Carlo Ancelotti’s Brazil squad this summer.

The good news for Chelsea is that João Pedro’s absence from the World Cup has given him plenty of time to recover ahead of the new campaign, and he looked thrillingly sharp in his second-half performance against Western Sydney Wanderers. The difference in class between João Pedro and Liam Delap, the man he replaced, was clear for all to see.

Two of the Brazilian’s three goals were classy, composed finishes — and he also created a goal for Gittens after surging past three defenders on the left wing. João Pedro looks like he means business.

News.title: China’s chip breakthrough triggers global tech rout
News.content:
China has achieved a breakthrough in developing technology crucial to the AI boom, overcoming US efforts to limit Beijing’s access to the systems.

China’s chip giant Shanghai Yuliangsheng has started production of deep ultraviolet lithography machines, according to The Information, a tech publication.

These machines, which can reach the size of a double-decker bus, use high-powered lasers to imprint designs on to silicon wafers, which are used to make chips.

Until recently, only Western companies and allies of the US had the capability to produce these machines.

The most advanced versions of the technology have largely been the preserve of companies such as Dutch giant ASML and Japan’s Nikon.

These machines have been cut off from China by US export controls, preventing their production of advanced chips as Washington seeks to slow the development of AI in the country.

Semiconductor stocks plunged on the report. Trading was briefly halted on South Korea’s benchmark Kospi index after it suffered a collapse of nearly 11pc overnight, following a bleak day on Wall Street.

Advanced semiconductors, such as those used in AI chips, rely on minuscule circuits, invisible to the naked eye. They can only be manufactured by directing tiny lasers onto microchip wafers, a process known as ultraviolet lithography.

News.title: Ramsay-Peaty ‘human first, athlete second’ as he settles for second bronze
News.content:
So a pair of bronze medals for the man who once only dealt in gold. Not that Adam Ramsay-Peaty thinks that is necessarily such a bad trade when he also computes the wider price of sporting domination.

“I’ve been that person who wins all the time, and it costs you pretty much everything, and I won’t say it’s worth it,” Ramsay-Peaty said after his return to international competition continued in his now favoured 50m breaststroke with a second podium place at these Commonwealth Games. “That period of time, where I was undefeated for eight years, it was athlete first, then human,” he added. “Now it’s human first, then athlete, which is a very fair price to pay.”

Aged 31, and with a baby girl on the way with wife Holly Ramsay, Ramsay-Peaty’s order of priorities might be understandable, but it was still another performance to raise questions over whether he can again climb to the top of a major podium.

Swimming is not kind to the over-30s – Michael Phelps was the first man in 2016 to win an Olympic gold in the pool even at the age Ramsay-Peaty is now – and we still have another two years until the Los Angeles Olympics. It would be the greatest achievement even of the Englishman’s extraordinary career to win his third individual Olympic title.

He trailed from the start here and was almost exactly a second outside his world record – set almost a decade ago – as Australia’s Sam Williamson completed a breaststroke double ahead of South Africa’s Michael Houlie in second. “As you get older, it gets harder,” said Ramsay-Peaty, before adding a crucial caveat, “but I’m enjoying it more…in my head, I’m getting fresher.”

News.title: Musk passed ‘slow death sentence’ on HIV patients by cutting US spending, says head of UNAIDS
News.content:
The world’s richest man has passed a “slow death sentence” on an untold number of people with HIV by cutting US spending on the disease, according to the head of UNAIDS.

In an interview with the Telegraph, Winnie Byanyima, executive director of the UN body, said Elon Musk’s claim that the cuts made to US aid had resulted in “zero” deaths was born of ignorance.

“I do not know where Elon Musk gets his data from, but he [is] showing ignorance of the disease”, Ms Byanyima told the Telegraph at the opening the 26th International Aids Conference in Rio de Janeiro.

“This disease is not like a bullet shot in the head and you die. This is an attack on the immune system.” Withdrawing medication is a “a slow death sentence,” she said.

Data released by UNAIDS show that reductions to international funding and cuts to HIV prevention and community services threaten a resurgence of the epidemic.

In 2025, 1.2 million more people became infected with HIV and 570 000 more people died of Aids-related illnesses as the world fell short of global targets.

Although new HIV infections and Aids-related deaths are at their lowest levels in more than 30 years, an 18 per cent cut to total international funding means previous gains are now at risk, say experts.

News.title: Europe faces energy crisis as gas stockpiles sink
News.content:
Britons face a winter of surging energy bills as Europe struggles to secure enough gas to fill its storage tanks.

A squeeze on Qatari gas shipments through the Strait of Hormuz has pushed European gas stockpiles into “energy crisis territory”, analysts at Wood Mackenzie warned.

The Continent’s storage tanks are barely 50pc full, a historical low for this time of year. Fresh tension between the US and Iran has cut the chances of more tankers sailing anytime soon.

Wood Mackenzie now forecasts that Europe will enter the winter with its gas storage tanks no more than 75pc full, compared with a five-year average of 90pc.

This could drive up prices, as Europe competes with Asia to buy extra gas, mostly from America on the spot market.

“Europe is approaching energy crisis territory,” Wood Mackenzie warned on Monday.

Meanwhile, Britain, which no longer stores significant amounts of gas, faces paying even more than rival buyers.

“The UK’s market model is that we’ll always pay more than anyone else, rather than relying on storage,” said David Lewis, an energy analyst at Wood Mackenzie.

“If other markets are going to struggle, it just means that the UK price will be even higher.”

Last week British Gas boss Chris O’Shea warned the country risked shortages over winter because of low levels of storage.

European gas prices fell at the fastest pace in a month on Monday after a pause in attacks between the US and Iran over the weekend, dropping to about €58 per megawatt hour.

Goldman Sachs expects the price to remain at about this level for the next three months, which is 80pc higher than the pre-war price of €32.

But the US investment bank warned the price could hit €100 next year if Middle East energy exports were slow to get back to normal.

The pressure from lost Qatari supply is being compounded by the EU’s plan to prohibit imports of Russian liquefied natural gas (LNG) from next year.

This will leave Europe in a bidding war with Japan and China for US LNG supplies.

Britain produces half its own gas and imports the rest, mostly via pipeline from Norway. But the Norwegian gas will largely track global LNG prices.

Laura Page, of the analysis firm Kpler, said Britain’s heavy reliance on Norway left it perilously exposed to any supply interruption.

“If there was a pipeline outage in Norway, or a problem with the gas field, that could cause prices to increase,” she said.

Mr Lewis said the Norwegians were postponing as much maintenance on their gas rigs as possible, to keep the supply flowing for Europe’s depleted stockpiles.

“But the problem is the same as in the UK: these are mature fields, they require a lot of maintenance, a lot of careful management,” he said.

Goldman Sachs said Europe had “only small room for error” in its gas stockpiling, and capacity could be as low as 28pc by the winter’s end.

Mr Lewis said the Netherlands and Germany were particularly exposed. “They might struggle to actually deliver the gas during peak demand days,” he said.

The El Nino weather pattern that will prevail for the rest of this year might come to Europe’s aid, delivering a milder winter than usual.

“It’s going to be an expensive winter unless we have a mild winter, which is what everybody’s hoping for at the moment. Fingers crossed,” Mr Lewis said.

Sports.title: Mo Salah’s future in limbo as European giants ‘WALK AWAY’ from transfer despite meeting with Liverpool icon three times
Sports.content:
MO SALAH has been handed a major blow after Besiktas claimed they have walked away from talks with the ex-Liverpool star.

The Egyptian is looking for his next club after leaving Anfield as a free agent at the end of the 2025-26 season.



Besiktas had emerged as a possible contender to sign the two-time Premier League winner despite links to Saudi Arabia.

But club chief Onder Ozen says the Turkish outfit have pulled out after a “deadlock” in negotiations, despite meeting Salah three times.



Ozen told the Turkish press, via the Daily Mail: “We contacted Salah, this also involved a financing model.

“Salah is a global star, a respected athlete. We met with Salah three times before the financial part of the negotiations was discussed.

“Up to this point, everything was smooth. When the financial side began, the initial smoothness slowed down from July 21st onwards.”

Ozen suggested Besiktas were unwilling to break their wage structure for Salah, who was earning around £400,000-a-week at Liverpool.

He reportedly pocketed an eye-watering £30.8million a year when performance-based bonuses were taken into account.

And Ozen said they simply couldn’t satisfy Salah’s massive demands while staying within their strict budget.



BEST ONLINE CASINOS – TOP SITES IN THE UK

He added: “Requests began to arrive that would both disrupt the flow of information and create a deadlock in the financial process. I can assume that a respected athlete like Salah was unaware of this.

“The club has a policy, and it cannot deviate from that policy, our President has very clearly identified his position and has stayed there.

“I don’t have a chance to say yes or no, Besiktas’s offer, made under its own terms, is clear. If a response comes to this offer, it can be evaluated.

“But Besiktas will not make another offer. They said they are also in talks with another club, maybe they will get a result from there.



“The last offer we made to Salah is the final point that does not harm Besiktas’s club identity.”

Salah left Liverpool as one of the club’s greatest ever players after netting 257 goals in 442 appearances across a nine-year spell.

He won two Premier League titles, two domestic cups and the Champions League during his time at the club.

But his final season at the club ended on a sour note after giving a bombshell interview in December accusing the club of “throwing him under the bus”.

Sports.title: Football lawmakers confirm new Fifa rule was WRONGLY used at World Cup as Argentina benefitted from error
Sports.content:
IFAB has admitted that VAR wrongly intervened on two instances of diving at the World Cup.

One of them helped Argentina squeeze past Switzerland in the quarter-finals, setting up their win over England in the semis.



Swiss forward Breel Embolo thought he had won a free-kick on the edge of the box following a tackle from Leandro Paredes.

But the VAR recommended an on-field review on the basis of ‘mistaken identity’.



Referee Joao Pinheiro then watched the footage, retracted the free-kick and showed a yellow card to Embolo – his second of the night – for simulation.

Ifab – global football‘s law-making body – has now confirmed that VAR intervention on grounds of ‘mistaken identity’ can only be used if there is doubt around the identity of the culprit.

It cannot spark a review of the offence itself, meaning Embolo should have remained on the pitch and the free-kick should have stood, if the rules were applied correctly.

The score was 1-1 when Embolo was dismissed in the 72nd minute, and Argentina went on to win 3-1 in extra-time.

The Ifab update reads: “A yellow card which is not a second yellow card can only be reviewed to identify the player who committed the offence that was penalised; the offence itself cannot be reviewed/changed.

“The use of the mistaken identity clause to deal with simulation during the World Cup was well received and will be included in the detailed review of the VAR protocol announced in circular No32.



BEST ONLINE CASINOS – TOP SITES IN THE UK

“However, it may not be used as such until that review is concluded.”

Argentina went on to lose in the final to Spain, but only after numerous instances of refereeing controversy, with beaten last-16 opponents Egypt even calling the tournament “rigged“.

The USA were the other team to benefit from a similar VAR mishap after Tim Ream was yellow carded for a tackle on Miguel Almiron in the group stage.

VAR cited ‘mistaken identity’ to recommend an on-field review, and ref Danny Makkelie reversed the decision before booking Almiron for diving.

Sports.title: Ipswich sign TALLEST player in Premier League history as 6ft 9in giant competes transfer to boost survival dream
Sports.content:
IPSWICH TOWN have signed the TALLEST player in Prem history after sealing a deal for 6ft 9in keeper Kjell Scherpen.

The towering shot-stopper, 26, has joined the Tractor Boys on a four-year deal from Belgian outfit Union Saint-Gilloise.



It’s a big move for Scherpen – quite literally – as he’s become the tallest star the English top flight has ever seen.

At 2.06 metres, he just about edges ex-Chelsea keeper Lucas Bergstrom (2.05m).



The biggest players in Premier League history previously were ex-Forest keeper Carlos Miguel, former Man City and Sunderland star Costel Pantilimon and Birmingham striker Nikola Zigic – who all stood 6ft 8in.

Even Peter Crouch is someway down the list at 6ft 7in, despite being thought of as one of the tallest to grace the top flight.

And Scherpen stands well clear of the current tallest stars too, including Illan Meslier and Dan Burn – both 6ft 7in – Nick Woltemade (6ft 6in) and Erling Haaland (6ft 5in).

Speaking after sealing his move to Portman Road, he said: “This is a very proud moment for me.

“This is a great opportunity for me to show my qualities and test myself in the best league in the world, so I’m really looking forward to making memories together.

Sports.title: Mia Khalifa, Piers Morgan and Samuel L. Jackson named in bizarre ‘Argentinophobia’ team by TV host after World Cup storm

He even organised the celebrities in a bizarre line-up as he struggled to come to terms with the World Cup heartbreak.



Viale said: “Mia Khalifa came out, a former pornographic actress, lecturing us on ethics and social justice.

“If Mia Khalifa goes to Iran and tries to preach her ideas there, she ends up hanging from a crane.

“So, frankly, replying to Mia Khalifa – she has zero standing or moral authority. Bye. Done.

“Piers Morgan said, ‘The Argentines are a bunch of thugs, violent, unpleasant and a disgrace to football’.



SUN VEGAS WELCOME OFFER: GET UP TO £100 BONUS

“Seriously, guys? We’re going to let a journalist run us down when his country occupied 14 territories, the Malvinas, Gibraltar, colonised half a continent?

“They are still hurt by Diego Maradona‘s left foot and Lionel Messi‘s right foot. They haven’t won a World Cup in 60 years.”

Khalifa made the cut after regularly rooting for the South American giants’ opponents during the tournament.

She claimed she would buy a Jude Bellingham kit after the Real Madrid superstar was spotted slapping Valentin Barco following England’s semi-final defeat.



And the three-time winners falling at the final hurdle allowed Khalifa to bag a huge amount of cash.

Torres‘ dramatic goal boosted her bank balance by a whopping £1.2MILLION after she made a mega-money bet backing Spain to come out on top.

Hollywood actor Samuel L. Jackson joined Khalifa and Morgan on the team sheet.

Viale hit out: “He thinks about life like a block of wood. He said that Argentina has historically been one of the most racist countries in the world, if not the most racist.



“We never had that kind of trouble here. I say this truly – this cheap, ignorant accusation is quite exhausting.

“Unfortunately in Argentina, we have many problems. There is corruption, poverty, backwardness, misery, shantytowns, displacement, insecurity, inflation. But there is no racism.”

RECOMMENDED STORIES

Viale also took aim at online streamers iShowSpeed and Ibai, along with Spanish singer Rosalia, actor Pedro Pascal, Mexican politician Claudia Sheinbaum and Mayor of New York City Zohran Mamdani.

Egypt boss Hossam Hassan was in the firing line as well – having claimed his side’s last-16 loss to Argentina was RIGGED.

Sports.title: Chelsea hoping to repeat Man Utd and Liverpool's inspired transfer deals with latest moves
Sports.content:
Chelsea have raised eyebrows in the market by going after Danny Welbeck and Jordan Henderson as Xabi Alonso throws a curveball with his recruitment plans.

The Blues have been associated with some of the most blockbuster transfers of the last five years, landing the likes of Enzo Fernandez, Moises Caicedo and Morgan Rogers for huge sums.

Rogers is their big capture of the summer, but as Alonso looks to put his stamp on a squad that floundered last season, finishing 10th, he's turned to some tried and tested Premier League performers who are certainly closing in on the ends of their careers.

Welbeck, now 35, is enjoying an Indian summer to his career and was seen as an outsider for England's World Cup squad. He's not played for a major side since leaving Arsenal in 2019, but could find his way back via Stamford Bridge.

‌



Chelsea want Jordan Henderson as Xabi Alonso lines up another shock signing READ MORE :

Chelsea line up shock Danny Welbeck swoop after Xabi Alonso green lights transfer READ MORE :

Not long after it emerged that Chelsea were working on a deal to land Jordan Henderson, another veteran performer at 36. The midfielder spent last year at Brentford after playing for in Saudi Arabia and the Netherlands, but clearly Alonso and Thomas Tuchel see something in him with the ex-Liverpool man part of the World Cup squad.

While such moves have been ridiculed they have more than worked in the past. Players are playing later and later now, without their level dropping. Just because its not a long-term investment, doesn't mean it can't work for the here and now.

Chelsea have ultimately underdelivered with their plan to continue investing in youth, which has got them nowhere for all the talk of potential and having the youngest squad in the league. Ultimately they need players who can get the job done.

View 4 Images Danny Welbeck could get one last big move to a top club (Image: GLYN KIRK, AFP via Getty Images)

‌



After all Henderson is a man who has lifted the Premier League and the Champions League during his career. Here are some cases of veteran moves that more than paid off for their club.

Zlatan Ibrahimovic to Man Utd

The Swede was a free agent after leaving PSG and decided to team back up with Jose Mourinho, who he'd worked with successfully at Inter Milan. Ibrahimovic was well into his 30s but had scored at an alarming rate whilst in Paris and decided to show he could crack it in England. He scored on debut and whilst the Red Devils didn't have their finest campaign Ibrahimovic didn't let his level drop. He finished with 28 goals - 17 more than his closest team-mate. He would also come up trumps, scoring the winner to claim the Community Shield and the Carabao Cup.

View 4 Images Zlatan Ibrahimovic claimed three trophies in his year at Man Utd

Gary McAllister to Liverpool

Then Reds boss Gerard Houllier was questioned when he signed a 35-year-old McAllister on a free after he'd left Coventry, especially when he had a young Steven Gerrard coming through the ranks. However he would prove a stroke of genius as Liverpool won their treble of trophies. His experience more than told and the Scotland midfielder was man of the match in the 2001 UEFA Cup final win over Alaves, scored a penalty winner against Barcelona in the semi-final before that and came up with an iconic 44-yard free-kick that won the Merseyside derby in stoppage time.

‌



Esteban Cambiasso to Leicester

He was 34 when he decided to call time on a decade at Inter, where he'd won five Serie A titles, four Coppa Italia crown and and a Champions League. The Argentine swapped that for newly promoted Leicester and would inspire late season form that kept them in the Premier League.

View 4 Images Esteban Cambiasso helped keep Leicester in the top flight (Image: Getty Images)

His first meaningful contribution saw him score in a comeback 5-3 win over the Red Devils. He was named Foxes Player of the Year after his impressive spell but chose not to sign a new deal with Leicester securing their historic title success the following year.

Jurgen Klinsmann to Tottenham

The German was by no means adored in England when he first rocked up at Tottenham in 1994 from Monaco. Klinsmann scored on his debut against Sheffield Wednesday and immediately won over supporters with a diving celebration, having been accused of the act previously. Klinsmann scored an amazing 30 goals in all competitions in his only season with Tottenham in his first spell. The forward then returned to Spurs at the age of 33 with Klinsmann’s goals saving the club from relegation after arriving in the winter.

‌



Claude Makelele to Chelsea

Maybe not in the peak veteran category having been 30 when he moved from Real Madrid, but their struggles after his exit showcased just how influential he was. The Blues flourished with the Frenchman at the base of their midfield and he effectively had a role and his position named after him, he was that good at it. He helped Chelsea win two Premier League titles during their first period under Jose Mourinho.

Sports.title: Bradley Barcola 'reaches verbal agreement' with Liverpool as blockbuster transfer advances
Sports.content:
Bradley Barcola 'reaches verbal agreement' with Liverpool as blockbuster transfer advances

Liverpool have made Bradley Barcola a top target and Reds manager Andoni Iraola spoken to the Paris Saint-Germain star, who's been valued at a jaw-dropping £145million

View 2 Images Bradley Barcola is keen to join Liverpool (Image: Chris Brunskill/Fantasista/Getty Images)

Bradley Barcola has reached an agreement in principle to join Liverpool after holding positive talks with Andoni Iraola. The Reds boss recently confirmed their plans to sign a winger and Barcola, 23, is a top target.

‌



The Frenchman be allowed to leave Paris Saint-Germain this summer for the right price. It's been reported that PSG will demand a staggering £145million for his signature.

‌



Now L'Equipe claim that Barcola has given his approval to the big-money move. However, Liverpool and PSG are still far away in their respective valuations of the ex-Lyon star.

‌



It comes after Premier League rivals Arsenal decided against pursuing Barcola. The Gunners are instead prioritising a stunning move for Real Madrid winger Vinicius Junior.

FOLLOW OUR LIVERPOOL FB PAGE! Latest Reds news and more on our dedicated Facebook page

Liverpool's Milos Kerkez explains why he chose to keep distance from Andy Robertson READ MORE :

Barcola has helped the French club win back-to-back Champions Leagues. Since joining PSG for around £38m in 2023, the winger has scored 39 goals and provided 35 assists in 152 appearances.

‌



During the World Cup, where he was in and out of France's starting XI, he revealed that he was uncertain about his future at club level. "I'm focused on the World Cup," Barcola said. "What happens after that, I don't know."

Meanwhile, Iraola told a press conference last week that Liverpool 'definitely need to sign a winger'. "When the market is open, you have to be always open to new options to improve the squad," the Reds boss explained.

Should Liverpool pay £145million for Bradley Barcola? Have your say in the comments section.

Iraola also said: "With the centre-back, with the right-back situation, in terms of defensive depth, we are, I think, very thin right now so I think it's a solution that we are trying to find, yes."

Sports.title: Ex-Liverpool star Glenn Hysen, 66, opens up after revealing he has Parkinson's disease
Sports.content:
Ex-Liverpool star Glenn Hysen, 66, opens up after revealing he has Parkinson's disease

Glenn Hysen, who made 72 appearances for Liverpool across three seasons and won two trophies, is now tackling Parkinson's after being diagnosed with a form of the disease

View 3 Images Glenn Hysen spent three years at Liverpool (Image: Mark Leech/Offside/Getty Images)

Former Liverpool centre-back Glenn Hysen has revealed that he has been diagnosed with Parkinson's disease. Hysen, 66, played at Anfield between 1989 and 1992.

‌



The Swede made 72 appearances for Liverpool, winning the First Division title in 1990. Hysen also won two UEFA Cups and five domestic trophies with Swedish giants Goteborg, where he's considered a legend.

‌



In an interview with Hant, the 68-time Sweden international and ex-captain confirmed that he'd been diagnosed with a mild form of Parkinson's. Thankfully, Hysen says that he is not expected to deteriorate provided that he continues taking medication.

‌



"I take medication three to four times a day with tablets," Hysen explained. "It's not dangerous, but you have to treat it."

FOLLOW OUR LIVERPOOL FB PAGE! Latest Reds news and more on our dedicated Facebook page

10 Liverpool deals that have changed the reputation of the Anfield transfer plan READ MORE :

Mohamed Salah transfer at risk of collapse as new club enters race for Liverpool legend READ MORE :

The 66-year-old also seems to be in good spirits. "I'm not the kind of person who digs deep into things," he continued. "I have no problem with it, it's not a big deal. I could probably work in a bar now and shake a drink."

‌



Hysen's symptoms flare up when he gets nervous, particularly in crowded areas where there are lots of people. "There are certain situations where you get a little nervous," he added. "If there are a lot of people around, I shake a little, but otherwise it's calm."

Liverpool marked the penultimate club in Hysen's decorated career. He made his professional debut for Goteborg in 1979 before joining Dutch heavyweights PSV Eindhoven four years later.

View 3 Images Glenn Hysen pictured in 2017 (Image: Michael Campanella/Getty Images)

‌



Hysen returned to Goteborg after a couple of seasons with PSV, continuing to have success with the club. Liverpool signed him after a spell with Serie A side Fiorentina, although he almost ended up at Manchester United.

United had invited Hysen over to England for a tour of Old Trafford and a fancy lunch, and it was expected that he would join the Red Devils in a £300,000 transfer move. Then-United manager Sir Alex Ferguson and chairman Martin Edwards personally flew out to Italy to seal the deal, only for his agent to tell them that he'd signed for Liverpool instead.

View 3 Images Glenn Hysen won two trophies in his first season at Liverpool (Image: Dan Smith/Allsport)

‌



Hysen made his debut for Liverpool in the 1989 Charity Shield, as Kenny Dalglish's men beat Arsenal 1-0 thanks to a first-half goal from Peter Beardsley. Hysen quickly established a partnership with Alan Hansen, forming the foundation of their First Division title win that season.

His Liverpool career came to an end under Graeme Souness, who sanctioned a free transfer to Swedish club GAIS. Hysen spent three years there before retiring in 1994.

Sports.content:
Bradley Barcola transfer timeline for Liverpool switch becomes clear during talks

Liverpool are reportedly in talks with Paris Saint-Germain over a potential deal for Bradley Barcola, although the fee being demanded is currently too high for the Reds

View 2 Images Bradley Barcola has been linked with a move to Liverpool (Image: Ian MacNicol/Getty Images)

Liverpool have been offered a hint that they may need to bide their time and wait for a deal for Bradley Barcola to be completed. The Anfield outfit have been heavily linked with a move for the Paris Saint-Germain star, as they look to strengthen their wide forward options.

‌



Mohamed Salah’s departure as a free agent, combined with the Achilles injury to Hugo Ekitike, means that Liverpool have been tipped to go into the market for reinforcements to their forward line.

‌



Victor Munoz remains the only new addition to the Liverpool squad this summer after the Spain international arrived in a £34.5million deal from Osasuna.

‌



A report from L'Equipe has claimed that Liverpool and PSG are presently in talks over a possible deal for Barcola, but notes that there remains a significant gap in valuation between the two sides.

FOLLOW OUR LIVERPOOL FB PAGE! Latest Reds news and more on our dedicated Facebook page

10 Liverpool deals that have changed the reputation of the Anfield transfer plan READ MORE :

The report suggests that Liverpool and PSG are prepared to remain patient regarding negotiations over a potential fee for Barcola, hinting that the transfer saga could continue throughout the remainder of the summer window.

‌



Separate reports have indicated that PSG value Barcola at approximately €170million (£145million), especially following Morgan Rogers' move to Chelsea in a £117million deal from Aston Villa.

Sandro Tonali and Elliot Anderson also sealed transfers for fees of at least £100million this summer.

The update follows reports which emerged over the weekend which claimed that Barcola had decided against signing a new contract with PSG, suggesting that a permanent move away from the Parc des Princes may be on the cards.

‌



View 2 Images Bradley Barcola has been linked with Arsenal and Liverpool (Image: (Photo by Patrick Smith - FIFA/FIFA via Getty Images))

The Athletic have also reported that PSG manager Luis Enrique only wants "committed" players in his squad next season, with indications that anyone reluctant to remain at the club may not get any minutes.

Consequently, this could suggest a possible repeat of events that unfolded before Alexander Isak joined Liverpool last summer.

‌



Liverpool ultimately struck a £125million agreement with Newcastle on deadline day, though only after several weeks of uncertainty that meant Isak didn't feature in any pre-season or Premier League fixtures for the Magpies ahead of his exit. The striker wasn't match-fit to begin following the transfer.

Isak went on to feature just 22 times for Liverpool in his first campaign for the club, and didn't make his first start for the club until September 17 against Atletico Madrid in the Champions League.

Sports.title: Liverpool's Milos Kerkez explains why he chose to keep distance from Andy Robertson
Sports.content:
Liverpool's Milos Kerkez explains why he chose to keep distance from Andy Robertson

Andy Robertson had to deal with Milos Kerkez coming in and taking his starting role at Liverpool with the Hungarian then having to manage his relationship with his former team-mate

View 2 Images Liverpool signed Milos Kerkez to ultimately replace Andy Robertson (Image: Getty Images)

Milos Kerkez admits he didn't shower Andy Robertson with love when he confirmed his Liverpool exit as he knew it would be an emotional time for the Scot.

‌



Robertson played 378 games for the Reds across his nine years and was a regular for the vast majority of those. He was a crucial player, especially under Jurgen Klopp, but Kerkez was essentially signed as his replacement with Robertson approaching the twilight years of his career.

‌



Immediately the ex-Bournemouth man came in as first choice and ended up playing 27 times, restricting Robertson to just 11 outings in the Premier League. He was linked with a January exit but remained until the end of the season before joining Tottenham.

‌



Robertson's exit was announced ahead of time and Kerkez concedes he kept an element of distance - but admits during the season they bounced ideas off of each other despite ultimately battling for the same position under Arne Slot.

10 Liverpool deals that have changed the reputation of the Anfield transfer plan READ MORE :

Mohamed Salah transfer at risk of collapse as new club enters race for Liverpool legend READ MORE :

The Hungarian defender told the Times on Robertson: “I didn’t want to get a lot on to him because he was a bit emotional as everything was coming to an end. I didn’t want to get on to him too much.

“But throughout the year he helped me. We had a few conversations about the crosses and about we need big lungs so we can run until tomorrow. We had conversations like that. Also, where to put the last ball, to focus, to put your head up and sometimes put better crosses in.

‌



“Andy helped me a lot, really and, like I said many times, he’s a legend. He’s someone I look up to. It’s not like I was held back or whatever because Andy was there. I always like to compete, it doesn’t matter who it is, and I’m going to push even more this year.”

View 2 Images Andy Robertson has moved to Tottenham as he eyes more involvement

Transitioning Robertson out of the side divided opinion, but he will now take his experience to north London as one of several impressive Tottenham signings this summer. Last term though he did open up on having to accept Liverpool's want to bring in younger players.

Article continues below

"The club has to move forward, the lads who have been here so long are not getting any younger. You have to accept it. I have had competition my whole career," he said midway through the campaign.

Sports.title: Xabi Alonso left with easy transfer decision as Chelsea win Western Sydney Wanderers goalfest
Sports.content:
For an hour in Sydney, Liam Delap was one of just a few established Chelsea players in a youthful team for the Blues' latest pre-season commitment.

When Delap left the field with Xabi Alonso's side 3-2 down, not only had he been outshone by a handful of Chelsea's army of teenage prodigies, but his replacement, Joao Pedro, emphasised why he is Chelsea's main man up front.

No sooner had he taken to the pitch, he had created the equalising goal for Jamie Gittens with some fine work. And the Brazilian then plundered the most rapid of hat-tricks in the dying embers of the game to ensure the Blues came out on top in a topsy-turvey game which finished 6-4.

In reality, there are plenty of reasons why Delap is likely to be among a number of players offloaded by Chelsea this summer, just 12 months after he was persuaded to pick the Blues ahead of numerous other top-flight suitors.

‌



It's a transfer that just hasn't worked out for either of the parties involved. And a parting of the ways probably benefits everyone, too.

Man Utd stance on hijacking Chelsea's Danny Welbeck transfer after secret talks READ MORE :

Chelsea line up shock Danny Welbeck swoop after Xabi Alonso green lights transfer READ MORE :

In fairness to Delap, he is far from the only Chelsea signing of the Blue Co era to have been scrutinised. In fact, while some have scoffed at the idea of adding a couple of elder statesman to the squad in the form of Danny Welbeck and Jordan Henderson, those moves, plus the failed pursuit of Granit Xhaka earlier in the summer, have started to convince people that the Blues have rediscovered their sanity in the transfer market after years of scattergun recruitment.

At 35, Welbeck certainly isn't coming in to lead the line for 38 games in the Premier League with all hopes of a title challenge pinned upon him. But he will be a very capable, and shrewd, deputy to Chelsea's first-choice No 9 in Pedro. And that means departures will be needed.

Where that leaves Delap, largely anonymous and goalless in an entertaining if messy goalfest here, is effectively no man's land.

‌



Bar a driving run and wild strike towards the end of the first half, Delap's impact was minimal and, as mentioned, it was some of his younger colleagues who really seized the opportunity to make an impression on their new manager. Dastan Satpayev, who does not officially join Chelsea until next month, gave Chelsea the lead with a neat finish after being played in. And it was 17-year-old Reggie Walsh who stole the show from midfield in the first half.

View 2 Images Liam Delap started the match up front for Chelsea but failed to impress with his future up in the air (Image: Darren Walsh/Chelsea FC)

With a deal for Welbeck advancing at speed, if ever there was a time for Delap to catch the eye, this was probably it. It's hard to see how he fits in with him, Pedro and Strasbourg's Emmanuel Emegha all vying for minutes this season.

Delap feels like the odd man out. Perhaps his selection here emphasised that; it wouldn't be a complete shock if he or the two other players with senior appearances he started with, Tosin Adarabioyo and Josh Acheampong were not involved in Alonso's immediate first-team plans, though the latter surely would not be offloaded permanently as he surely has a future at Stamford Bridge.

‌



For Delap, the writing was already on the wall. And nothing he did in Sydney is likely to change that.

Sports.title: Why has Hamilton received so many penalties and what have they cost him?
Sports.content:
Lewis Hamilton has received four penalties from the stewards in the last three Formula 1 race weekends - an unusually high number for any driver over such a short period.

After his latest penalty in Sunday's Hungarian Grand Prix for speeding in the pit lane, Hamilton stated on the radio that the stewards are "handing out penalties like crazy".

The result was that Hamilton lost further crucial points in the title race, and he now trails Kimi Antonelli by 50 points in the Drivers' Championship, so have the penalties been justified?

Image: The F1 Drivers' Championship with 11 rounds remaining

British Grand Prix - false start

Finishing Position: Third

Points lost: Likely none

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player New angles of Lewis Hamilton's false start at British GP

Hamilton was handed a five-second time penalty for jumping the start at the British Grand Prix when he was deemed to be creeping forward before the lights went out.

He went on to finish third, perhaps fortunately after knocking down his pit mechanic at a late pit stop, so the penalty likely did not impact his result. Hamilton considered the penalty harsh.

"We talked in the drivers' briefing the fact that they're inconsistent with this stuff. Drivers in the past have moved and not been penalised," he said.

"We discussed that, as long as you're not moving when the last lights are on, you shouldn't be penalised. I wasn't out of my box. And they agreed. So they're looking into that for the future."

Belgian Grand Prix - causing a collision

Finishing Position: Fourth

Points lost: Up to six

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Mercedes driver George Russell spins after contact with Lewis Hamilton and his race ends on the opening lap, but was the Ferrari driver's penalty fair?

Hamilton was given a five-second time penalty for being "wholly at fault" for colliding with George Russell on the opening lap of the British Grand Prix at Turn 5.

On the inside line, Hamilton understeered into Russell and was "unable to maintain sufficient separation" which led to the contact and Russell spinning into the gravel and out of the race.

But, Russell himself said the contact was a "racing incident" even though he came off worse.

Hamilton said: "Even the driver I collided with said that it was just a racing incident. I think that one was not needed. But that cost me a lot of points."

Hamilton benefited from pitting and serving his penalty under a Virtual Safety Car, but without the penalty he would almost certainly have been on the podium rather than finishing fourth.

He may even have had a fighting chance of victory given his team-mate Charles Leclerc was only overtaken by race-winner Antonelli with 10 laps to go. A battle with Leclerc was definitely on the cards for second.

Hungarian Grand Prix Qualifying - impeding

Starting Position: Fifth

Impact: Potential to lead race and fight for win

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Lewis Hamilton's was given a grid penalty for blocking Oscar Piastri in qualifying in Hungary

Hamilton was hit with a three-grid place penalty for impeding Oscar Piastri during the final part of Qualifying at the Hungarian Grand Prix.

After completing his final Q3 run, where he did not improve, Hamilton was not told Piastri was starting his flying lap, so effectively blocked the McLaren driver through Turn 1.

"That was really just unfortunate. I take responsibility for ultimately being on track. I should have looked in my mirrors," said Hamilton.

"But I thought everyone would have been at the end of the first lap. The information I got was right at the end. A communication error."

Hamilton was not happy that Ferrari sent himself and Leclerc out first for the last Q3 runs, which partly led to the impeding incident with Piastri.

He had qualified second and, with brand-new soft tyres, would have had a golden chance to take the lead on the first lap and potentially win the race. Instead, he started fifth and was penalised again in the Grand Prix.

Hungarian Grand Prix - speeding in the pit lane

Finishing Position: Fourth

Points lost: Up to three

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Anthony Davidson analyses Lewis Hamilton's speeding in the pit lane that handed him a five-second time penalty

The final race before the summer break was not well executed by Ferrari and Hamilton, who endured a difficult time after being overtaken by Max Verstappen after the first round of pit stops.

But Hamilton was still potentially on course for second until a Virtual Safety Car with 13 laps to go led Ferrari to pit for new fresh tyres.

In the pit lane, Hamilton exceeded the 80kph speed limit by 0.1kph as he was eager to beat Antonelli on the merge between pit exit and track.

It was a driver mistake but Hamilton thought, with hindsight, he should not have pitted and would have been third without the stop.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Max Verstappen shocks Lewis Hamilton with a stunning overtake at the Hungarian Grand Prix

"The call came literally just before the pit lane entry and I didn't have time to debate and you've got to trust the decision that has been taken," he told Sky Sports F1.

"In hindsight, my tyres were totally fine. I was probably going to lose out to Max but I think I could have kept third at least. Then just opened up the door to obviously the penalty that I got in the end."

Hamilton: I can't give stewards any reason to penalise me

Apart from the Belgium collision with Russell, all of Hamilton's penalties are hard, or impossible, to argue against. He has probably only lost six points from the in-race penalties but the impeding in Qualifying at the Hungaroring was the most detrimental.

Ferrari had great pace in Budapest and track position is king, so a good start on softs from the front row of the grid likely would have seen Hamilton in the lead.

His raw speed has been very strong recently, too, so victory was possible on Sunday and he would have been less than 40 points behind Antonelli.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Lewis Hamilton responds to his speeding penalty from Budapest

Ferrari and Hamilton must cut out these unforced errors if they want that record-breaking eighth world drivers' title.

"I'll work hard to try and come back. There's still a lot of positives to take. I'm going to try and make sure I don't give them any reason to penalise me," said Hamilton.

Sports.title: Mithaaly chases first success at Yarmouth
Sports.content:
We have a busy day’s racing on Tuesday with flat action from Ffos Las and Yarmouth, live on Sky Sports Racing...

3.10 Yarmouth - Eye-catching Shadwell debutant Mithaaly and Godolphin newcomer Noble Prince clash

The George Boughey-trained Mithaaly and Charlie Appelby's newcomer Noble Prince should be competitive in the British Stallion Studs EBF Novice Stakes.

Mithaaly caught the eye at Windsor when staying on very well after getting a touch outpaced two furlongs out.

The extra furlong looks sure to suit and this 260,000gns yearling sets a solid standard.

Godolphin-owned Frankel colt Noble Prince could go well on debut with trainer Charlie Appleby posing an impressive record of 13 from 29 (45 per cent) with two-year-olds this year.

Debutant Majestic Jude could pose the chief threat being half-brother to the precocious 2021 Group Two Prix Robert Papin winner Atomic Force, as Note To Self has progressed with each run this season, narrowly placing second by a head at Windsor.

6.30 Ffos Las - Flyta headlines competitive five-runner handicap

The in-form Flyta sets the standard in the Dragonbet / Martin Davies Handicap.

Flyta broke her maiden tag last month over course and distance following a promising effort at Windsor.

She seems the most likely to score here with another easy lead potentially afforded.

Course and distance winner Sofian can be competitive after the saddle slipped following a break last time out.

Name The Day must go much better after shaping amiss at Newbury as once promising debut winner Distinct Sprit is proving consistent in the search for his first win since.

Bahraini jockey, Ebrahim Nader rides.

7.30 Ffos Las - Noble Style's full-sister Summerson features

A small but select field go to post in the Maiden Fillies' Stakes.

Noble Style's full-sister Summerson marginally sets the standard as she stayed on gamely to finish runner-up to Sandringham ninth, Crownright.

Being full-sister to the flashy Gimcrack winner does not point to this longer trip but also being a half-sister to highly tried 12-furlong filly, Little Dorrit, coupled with how she kept on at Chester, means there is potential for more improvement with the extra distance.

Full-sister to useful two-year-old, Seacruiser, Seacole has run well on two starts and is sure to be suited by 12-furlongs.

Cracking Beauty is bred for longer trips. She was caught too far back at Kempton but stayed on well and should improve again where she can be seen to greater effect.

Best of the rest

5.25 Yarmouth - Thapa VC headlines.

Sports.title: Joao Pedro nets hat-trick as Chelsea score SIX in Alonso's first game
Sports.content:
Joao Pedro scored a nine-minute hat-trick as Xabi Alonso began his Chelsea reign with a ridiculous 6-4 victory over Western Sydney Wanderers in pre-season.

Chelsea led through 17-year-old Dastan Satpaev in only the sixth minute, yet managed to fall behind three times to the A-League side before substitute Joao Pedro showed his class with a late treble in Sydney.

Alonso named a youthful side in a 4-2-3-1 formation with Tosin and Liam Delap the only significant senior experience in the starting XI before introducing the likes of Cole Palmer, Joao Pedro, Estevao and Levi Colwill midway through the second half.

How Chelsea lined up First half (4-2-3-1): Sharman-Lowe; Acheampong, Subuloye, Tosin, Emenalo; Watson, Essugo; Kavuma-McQueen, Walsh, Satpaev; Delap.

From the 64th minute: Sanchez; Palestra, Colwill, Fofana, Anselmino; Watson, Nicoll-Jazuli; Estevao, Palmer, Gittens; Joao Pedro.

Chelsea's first two goals, the second coming from Dario Essugo, were brilliant moves from back to front on a bumpy pitch used primarily for rugby league matches, and were a sign of the style Alonso will hope to implement at Stamford Bridge.

But their defending was poor and after being level at the break, Alonso's side were trailing in the 64th minute by the time he brought on his stars, deploying Palmer in the No 10 role with Estevao on the right and Jamie Gittens on the other side.

Gittens levelled two minutes after his introduction for 3-3, yet Estevao's slack pass left youngster Reggie Watson short deep inside their own half, and Western Sydney substitute Awan Lual punished the error to restore their lead with little over 10 minutes remaining.

But then the Joao Pedro show started. He finished expertly from inside the box to bring Chelsea level again, slotted home to give them the lead after being played in by Palmer and then tapped in his third from a couple of yards at a corner to seal a remarkable hat-trick and the win.

What did we learn from Alonso's debut?

Sky Sports' Ron Walker:

There's always a word of caution about reading too much into the opening game of pre-season, especially with so many first-team players missing for Chelsea.

But there are certainly a few takeaways from Xabi Alonso's debut in the dugout...

Flexible formation - Chelsea defended in a four but with the ball, Landon Emenalo bombed forward down the left and often overlapped Dastan Satpaev down that flank. It did leave Chelsea open at the back, though.

Chelsea defended in a four but with the ball, bombed forward down the left and often overlapped Dastan Satpaev down that flank. It did leave Chelsea open at the back, though. Youngsters impress - Both Reggie Watson and Reggie Walsh looked sharp and linked up well in midfield, with the former the only player to complete 90 minutes. Mahdi Nicoll-Jazuli also enjoyed a bright half-time cameo while Dastan Satpaev started brightly but faded

Both and looked sharp and linked up well in midfield, with the former the only player to complete 90 minutes. also enjoyed a bright half-time cameo while started brightly but faded First-teamers' sharpness - A number of Chelsea regulars only got half an hour to show their stuff but Cole Palmer and Joao Pedro looked immediately up to speed and had little rust to shake off. You can't argue with a nine-minute hat-trick

A number of Chelsea regulars only got half an hour to show their stuff but and looked immediately up to speed and had little rust to shake off. You can't argue with a nine-minute hat-trick Defensive concerns - Josh Acheampong and Tosin were two of Chelsea's more senior players to start the game in Sydney but both found life difficult against a side who finished bottom of the A-League last season. They were offered little cover by the visitors' midfield at times.

Alonso: We need to manage games better

Chelsea head coach Xabi Alonso said:

"It has been a very useful friendly that we can learn a lot from today. There were moments when we were struggling to find solutions, and we needed this. The positive is that we corrected them, but there were moments when the game management is something that we can learn from today.

"When they were pressing so high, it was tough to find the solution from inside, to have a different understanding of what's happening, and to make those changes in the game.

"It's something that will happen often in all the games, and the more situations we struggle with and find solutions, the better team we will be. For that, I think that this friendly is going to be useful for the future, and as well for minutes for everyone."
