Chelsea have held talks with the Brighton forward Danny Welbeck (35) and are also keen to sign Jordan Henderson (36). Welbeck knocked in 13 Premier League goals for the Seagulls last season and was fancied as a possible option for England at the World Cup, while Henderson made the cut, only to suffer a freak wrist injury. Chelsea are presumably drawing up eight-year contracts for both veterans.

In Germany, Borussia Dortmund have agreed to sign the midfielder Konstantinos Karetsas from Racing Genk in Belgium, for a fee that could rise to £32m.

And John Stones, a free agent after leaving Manchester City, has moved closer to completing his move to Inter as reported in these pages: a deal has been verbally agreed.

Sports.title: Mind the ever-growing gap: the Premier League keeps spending big
Sports.content:
The financial power of the Premier League is unmatched. The teams in England’s top division have collectively invested more than £1.4bn in new players already this summer (through disclosed fees alone), around £303m more than the 76 clubs from the Bundesliga, La Liga, Ligue 1 and Serie A combined.

These figures are the gross spend, so take no account of players sold to help balance the books. Factoring this in only increases the divide. The clubs of Ligue 1 and the Bundesliga are £203.4m and £72.2m in credit from their transfer dealings respectively. While La Liga (£163.1m) and Serie A (£124.1m) have spent more than they have earned, they are an ocean adrift of the Premier League’s net spend of £523.6m.

None of this is new; it has been the trend for many years. The worrying aspect for teams across the continent is that the gap between the Premier League and the rest may grow wider before the summer is out.

Despite their enormous outlay, top-flight English teams have spent about £230m less than Premier League clubs of 2025-26 had at this point last year. But only 25 deals were completed by the end of 1 July (which is when new contracts usually start, explaining why pre-arranged moves are often finalised then). It’s roughly half as many as the 47 that occurred by that date last summer. The expanded World Cup will probably have delayed some deals, creating a potential backlog of transfer spending that will soon hit the books.

Assessing clubs individually highlights why most might continue spending. Aston Villa, Brighton and Tottenham have already spent more in gross terms than in the entirety of the summer 2025 transfer window. Unai Emery has a net £109.6m burning a hole in his pocket following business which includes the departures of Morgan Rogers and Youri Tielemans. Brighton will need a larger squad as they have a Conference League campaign on the horizon while Tottenham are hoping to improve upon consecutive 17th-place finishes. Their trading may not be complete even though they’ve already outspent their efforts from last summer, with Spurs’ net spend of £149.7m the highest in Europe’s big five leagues.

Chelsea also have a higher net spend than last year, even before their reportedly agreed deal for Crystal Palace’s Maxence Lacroix goes through. Even if that transfer is not completed, would you bet against BlueCo throwing more money around, especially with a new manager to back? Danny Welbeck is the latest to emerge on the Stamford Bridge radar. Either way, Chelsea have already invested more in new talent than they had on this day last year. The same is true for Everton, Fulham, Manchester City and Newcastle, all of whom may have further incomings in the pipeline, too.

There are other clubs with work to do. The three promoted teams have only spent £8m more between them than Sunderland alone had at this point in 2025. Régis Le Bris added a total of 18 new players to his squad last summer, with fellow promoted sides Burnley (15) and Leeds (11) also hitting double figures for incomings. By these standards, Ipswich (with seven new players), Hull (four) and Coventry (three) must recruit further.

At the opposite end of the Premier League scale, Arsenal, Liverpool and Manchester United have collectively spent two-thirds of a billion less on new talent than they did last summer. The latest rumour mill gossip says the champions may make a move for Vinícius Júnior. If not the Brazilian then perhaps Bradley Barcola, though Liverpool are also said to be pursuing the Paris Saint-Germain winger. Neither player will be remotely cheap. United are believed to be targeting Ollie Watkins – he wouldn’t cost Vinícius or Barcola money, but neither would Villa sell to a rival at a reduced fee.

The Premier League also has clubs who have yet to make an outlay. It is unlikely Crystal Palace, Nottingham Forest and Sunderland end the summer without spending a transfer fee as is now the case. It would be remiss of Palace and Sunderland not to invest when they are in European competition this season. As for Forest, like Chelsea they have had an insatiable thirst for player turnover in recent times. With Elliot Anderson having left for an enormous fee, replacements will surely arrive soon.

It is remarkable to think the Premier League may not be halfway through its summer outlay when £1.4bn has already been used for recruitment. The top-flight English clubs collectively spent £3.1bn on players last summer, with over £600m in the final week of dealing alone. That figure may be blown away by the time the transfer window closes on 3 September.

Sports.title: Fifa president Gianni Infantino called to appear before Congress over Trump ties
Sports.content:
Jamie Raskin, the top Democrat on the House judiciary committee, has launched an investigation into Fifa president Gianni Infantino, seeking documents that would detail the ties between soccer’s governing body and Donald Trump and his administration.

In a Sunday letter, Raskin wrote to Infantino and called for Fifa to provide any documents and communications related to gifts, payments or benefits provided to Trump and his associates, as well as the visitor logs for Fifa’s office space in Trump Tower, which it acquired last year. The committee also requested that Infantino sit for a transcribed interview.

Infantino’s relationship with Trump came under scrutiny in the lead-up to this summer’s World Cup. In December, at the World Cup draw in Washington, Trump was awarded a newly created “Fifa peace prize” at the Kennedy Center, where renovations were allegedly “rushed” on the administration’s orders to prepare for the event. Fifa opened its office in Trump Tower in midtown Manhattan last July.

Such scrutiny intensified during the World Cup. Trump made several calls to Infantino to lobby for a review of US striker Folarin Balogun’s controversial red-card suspension before the Americans’ last-16 match against Belgium. Fifa did reverse Balogun’s ban, but the political circus cast a pall over the US team and drew the ire of other teams and associations from around the world.

Alongside the leaders of Canada and Mexico, Trump joined Infantino for the World Cup trophy presentation after Spain beat Argentina in the final. The pair, who watched the final together in a glassed-in section of luxury seats, were met with boos from the New York New Jersey Stadium crowd when they took the field.

Raskin’s letter references the Department of Justice’s decision to “dismiss the indictments” of defendants in US government investigations into corruption in global soccer, including the 2015 prosecution of more than 20 high-level Fifa officials and sports-marketing executives.

“[Y]our election as Fifa president was supposed to mark a red-card break from a decades-long culture of corruption and scandals that dressed down world soccer’s reputation,” Raskin wrote to Infantino in the letter. “Instead, at the start of your tenure, you dismantled Fifa’s ethical guardrails and disabled the organization’s ethics committee by pushing out most of its members. This lack of transparency and oversight has since paved the way for you to ingratiate yourself with the Trump administration via tactics that a New York University law professor and one of your former ethics committeemen described as ‘legal bribery’.”

The letter also addresses Fifa’s World Cup ticketing policy, which is already the subject of investigations by several attorneys general in the United States. The use of dynamic pricing drew much criticism during the tournament, leading to massive surges and pricing out many fans from attending games.

“The most recent quid pro quo that Fifa and President Trump orchestrated is not a victimless crime. It hurts Americans. Fifa has taken its newfound favored status in the Trump administration as a sign that it may rip off its consumers, most notably, by employing illegal price-gouging and fraudulent sales tactics for the World Cup,” Raskin said in the letter.

The letter gives a deadline of 9 August to provide the requested documents and schedule the interview. Raskin does not have the power to compel Infantino to appear, given that Democrats do not hold the majority in the House, unless he garners Republican support.

Fifa’s interactions with the US government did not end with this summer’s World Cup. The US is expected to be the primary host of the Women’s World Cup in 2031, and the success of this year’s tournament has led many to speculate that the 2038 men’s World Cup could be hosted by the US. Fifa has been approached for comment.

Earlier on Monday, Infantino used a 15-part message on Instagram to denounce his critics, accusing them of spreading hate and false narratives. He touted the World Cup as a success.

More than 200 Fifa members have endorsed Infantino ahead of the presidential election in March, but some associations have stood in opposition. The Norwegian football federation is planning to submit a formal complaint to Fifa ethics investigations over Trump’s role in the reversal of Balogun’s ban.

Sports.title: Chelsea’s new-look XI with five summer signings including Danny Welbeck and Jordan Henderson
Sports.content:
Danny Welbeck and Jordan Henderson could bring much-needed experience to a youthful Chelsea side for the upcoming season.

Following a campaign in which the Blues finished outside the European spots in tenth place, new boss Xabi Alonso was tasked with a major revamp of his squad.

8 Alonso has been tasked with bringing European football back to Stamford Bridge Credit: Getty

The west London outfit have been one of the Premier League's busiest sides this window - scouring Europe for some of the best young talent on offer.

Morgan Rogers was snapped up from Aston Villa in a £117million deal - becoming the most expensive British player in history.

Chelsea also forked out £47m on right-back Marco Palestra from Serie A side Atalanta.

Meanwhile, teenage winger Geovany Quenda has officially linked up in a £42m transfer - one year after the move was agreed with Sporting Lisbon.

And striker Emmanuel Emegha has finally arrived from sister club Strasbourg for around £21m having thrashed out an agreement in September.

Those four players will soon be joined by Maxence Lacroix, with the Crystal Palace centre-back closing in on a £55m switch.

Chelsea Pensioners

With BlueCo making it their mission to bring in highly-rated youngsters since their £4.25bn takeover in 2022, they are set to completely go against their model.

On Monday, it was reported how Chelsea are poised to bring in striker Welbeck from Brighton and midfielder Henderson from Brentford.

With a combined age of 71, the two veteran England internationals are unlikely to challenge for a regular starting spot.

Instead, they will likely be utilised as adept back-ups while providing support for their younger teammates - both off and on the pitch.

8 Welbeck enjoyed the most productive Premier League season of his career in the 2025/26 campaign Credit: talkSPORT

8 Henderson returned to England last summer to join Brentford after departing Ajax Credit: Getty

Chelsea fielded the youngest average age [23.4] of any Premier League side in single match in the 2025/26 season.

In fact, Chelsea put out nine of the youngest 12 line-ups in the top-flight and 13 of the youngest 18.

Blues content creator Alex Harris gave his seal of approval on the potential signings when commenting on Welbeck and Henderson to talkSPORT.

He said: "Look, these guys are not going to be starters for us, they're going to be players that come in, try and help the younger guys, and they'll fill in every now and then, one of our issues is we have no experience."

Before adding: "This is major for us and it is extreme, but we've been extreme in terms of not signing players with any experience.

"So why do I not mind Jordan Henderson and Danny Welbeck? Because I don't mind either of them, to be honest with you.

8 Chelsea splashed out £117m on Rogers to make him their record signing Credit: Getty

"Because number one, I know they're not going to play every week, number two, they're winners, they've been part of winning sides and that's what we need.

"We need people who know how to win, we need people who are going to be someone for the younger players to speak to and go, 'Well, how did you deal with this and that?'"

With a raft of incomings already confirmed at Stamford Bridge and more on the way, here talkSPORT.com takes a look at two ways Chelsea could start under Alonso.

How could Chelsea start under Alonso?

Keeping his place between the sticks will likely be Robert Sanchez, who has made 90 outings for the club across the last two years.

Skipper Reece James will continue to deputise at right-back, with Jorell Hato to potentially slot in on the other side of defence following Marc Cucurella's £51.8m move to Real Madrid.

And Lacroix is expected to come into the heart of defence to partner Cobham academy Levi Colwill.

8 Lacroix is closing in on a move fro Chelsea from London rivals Crystal Palace Credit: Getty

Should Enzo Fernandez remain at Chelsea amid uncertainty over his future, he would play next to Moises Caicedo in central midfield.

Cole Palmer could then be used in a No.10 role, allowing Brazilian sensation Estevao to feature on the right wing, with Rogers to be deployed on the left flank.

And Joao Pedro would surely lead the line ahead of Welbeck after finishing at Chelsea's top scorer with 20 goals last campaign.

The duo are poised to be teammates for a third time having played together at Watford and Brighton.

8 Rogers could be deployed as a left winger under Alonso

Chelsea alternative XI

Should Alonso decide to ring the changes, he could elect to start five summer recruits.

Two changes could be made in defence from his likely preferred line-up with a reshuffle in the full-back positions.

James could be replaced by Palestra, while natural right-back Malo Gusto could come in at left-back instead of Hato, having played there three times in the previous campaign.

Henderson could then come in for Fernandez in midfield, with Rogers to move from the left wing into the No.10 role, with Alonso hailing his versatility at a recent press conference.

Commenting on the 23-year-old, he said: "One of his best qualities is that he is flexible.

"He plays in that pocket position, close to the striker, close to our No.10 – but he has also played on the right side even though he is more used to coming from the left."

8 Palestra spent the 2025/26 term on loan at Bolgona, with his performances seeing him make his Italy debut in March Credit: Getty

Palmer could then slot in on the right, with Pedro Neto to come in on the left wing.

And Welbeck may on occasion be favoured ahead of Pedro up top, with the 35-year-old coming off the back of the best goalscoring season of his career.

Welbeck fired in 14 goals in all competitions, with 13 strikes coming in the Premier League - the second term in a row he achieved double digits.

Sports.title: Chelsea told to make audacious swoop for Harry Kane after change in transfer policy
Sports.content:
Chelsea told to make audacious swoop for Harry Kane after change in transfer policy

Chelsea have been told they could be the 'perfect' move for Harry Kane amid their shift in transfer strategy.

The Blues are pushing to bolster their squad with experienced Premier League veterans ahead of the new season.

3 Chelsea's new transfer strategy could make them the 'perfect' move for Kane Credit: Getty

Xabi Alonso's side are currently working on deals for both Jordan Henderson and Danny Welbeck, talkSPORT understands.

Chelsea lead the race to sign Henderson on a free transfer from Brentford.

Meanwhile, Brighton striker Welbeck has already agreed personal terms with the club.

Kane has now been put forward as a potential signing after entering the final 12 months of his current Bayern Munich deal.

Chelsea 'perfect' for Kane

Andy Goldstein and Andy Townsend discussed a possible move to Stamford Bridge during Tuesday's Breakfast show.

Asked if Chelsea would be the 'perfect' move for Kane due to their new strategy, Townsend explained: "If his contract is up, they’re going to have to renegotiate now.

"They wouldn’t want to let Harry leave for nothing because he would still have a serious transfer fee attached to him.

"Look, it’s an interesting one with Harry, he is such a consistent goalscorer. What he’s done in Munich is pretty remarkable, really.

"He’s put himself on the same level as (Cristiano) Ronaldo and (Lionel) Messi when he’s getting 60 and 70 (goals) in a season. That’s incredible.

"So who wouldn’t be interested in taking Harry Kane at the moment?"

3 Kane, who turned 33 on Tuesday, is into the final year of his current Bayern deal. Credit: Getty

Kane's record scoring form

Since joining Bayern from Tottenham Hotspur in 2023, Kane has scored 146 goals in 147 appearances for the club.

Those include 61 strikes in all competitions last season as he won a third consecutive Bundesliga golden boot.

The England captain, who turned 33 on Tuesday, also scored six times at the World Cup to extend his record tally for the Three Lions to 85 goals in 121 caps.

Kane also remains the Premier League's second-highest scorer of all-time behind Alan Shearer with 213 goals in 320 appearances.

As for whether a move to Chelsea would work for all parties, Townsend added: "The thing with Harry, unlike Danny Welbeck is coming to Chelsea knowing that he’s going to play but he’s not going to play every week.

"Harry wants to play every week. He would expect to start absolutely every game."

3 Joao Pedro is Chelsea's only senior striker not facing an uncertain future this summer Credit: Getty

Chelsea striker latest

Welbeck's potential move to Chelsea would bolster the club's striker options but may not be the last centre-forward signing they make this summer.

Joao Pedro is the only current senior striker at Stamford Bridge without any uncertainty surrounding his future.

Chelsea are open to offers for both Liam Delap and Emmanuel Emegha, who only joined the club from Strasbourg this summer.

Meanwhile, Nicolas Jackson was previously offered to Aston Villa following his return from a season-long loan at Bayern.

Marc Guiu has also been linked with a move away from the Blues this summer.

Fellow striker David Datro Fofana has made just four first-team appearances since joining Chelsea in January 2023 and is fresh from a fifth loan spell away from west London.

Sports.title: Premier League players who will be ‘like a new signing’ in 2026/27
Sports.content:
Premier League players who will be ‘like a new signing’ in 2026/27

It's a phrase that Premier League fans have heard a thousand times every time any player returns from injury - 'He's like a new signing'.

However, in the most extreme cases of long-term absentees, it really will feel like a blast from the past for some supporters this season.

8 Tottenham's Dejan Kulusevski has missed over a year of football Credit: Getty

On the opposite end of the scale, there will be several players set to miss the majority of the 2026/27 campaign through injury.

Tottenham playmaker Xavi Simons was left 'heartbroken' after a serious knee problem in April put him out for the foreseeable future.

Liverpool striker Hugo Ekitike is out for nine months, having ruptured his Achilles against Paris Saint-Germain earlier that same month.

Manchester United's Manuel Ugarte is also facing up to a year on the sidelines after sustaining a knee ligament injury at the World Cup.

The positive for those clubs is that the solution is not always found in the transfer market but rather in a successful treatment room.

Premier League players ‘like a new signing’

Fábio Carvalho - Brentford

The 23-year-old has so far struggled to show why Brentford signed him from Liverpool in a deal worth £27.5million in 2024.

Carvalho, once compared to Philippe Coutinho, managed just two goals in 19 Premier League games in his first year in west London.

In his defence, only three of those appearances came as a start - and his fortunes didn't change under Keith Andrews last season either.

8 Carvalho has made 33 appearances for Brentford in all competitions Credit: Getty

Carvalho played just six times in the Premier League in 2025/26 (one start) before sustaining an ACL injury in November.

Brentford head coach Andrews said: "It's been a tough week for him; it's devastating. He did it around a week ago in training.

"He's someone I have a lot of respect for as a man.

"I have felt for him this season - he hasn't been given as much of an opportunity as we would have ideally liked to have given him. He knows that, and we've been in constant communication about his development and ambitions as a player.

"Unfortunately, that's been taken away from him for a period of time. But we'll support him really well, like we always do. Fábio knows he'll get the support from everyone at the football club, including me, throughout this difficult period."

Carvalho missed the rest of the season through injury, but is expected to return in the early months of the upcoming campaign.

8 Carvalho's highlight of last campaign was a late equaliser against Chelsea Credit: Getty

Stefanos Tzimas - Brighton

The 20-year-old's return from an ACL injury could be especially timely with Danny Welbeck agreeing terms on a move to Chelsea.

The Greek striker was called an 'exceptional young talent' by Brighton boss Fabian Hurzeler after his £21m arrival from Nuremberg last year.

He was forced to wait for his chances, with his first eight Premier League appearances coming from the substitutes' bench.

Tzimas scored his first English top-flight goal in a 2-0 win at Nottingham Forest, and was rewarded with his first start, where he cruelly suffered a serious knee injury in a 3-4 home loss to Aston Villa.

But Brighton revealed at the start of July that the Greece under-21 international is back in training for pre-season.

8 Tzimas had only just been starting to show Brighton fans his top level before the injury curse struck Credit: Getty

Tzimas boasted three goals and two assists in 12 appearances across all competitions before his injury in December

Cheick Doucoure - Crystal Palace

The 26-year-old has had a more torrid time than most with his injury issues curtailing most of the past two and a half years.

Doucoure's stock was at an all-time high in 2023, when he was voted Palace's player of the year and attracted interest from Liverpool.

The Eagles held onto their prized midfield asset, but the Malian has played just 13 senior games since his first injury that November.

Doucoure ruptured his Achilles and then sustained a torn meniscus in his knee that has meant he didn't play a minute last season.

Palace's No.28 last appeared for the first-team on January 15, 2025 at Leicester City, and ended a 14-month absence for the U21s this March.

In what is a huge boost for new boss Pierre Sage, Doucoure has been able to play in both of Palace’s first two pre-season fixtures thus far.

8 Doucoure signed for Palace from RC Lens in 2022 - the same club new boss Sage has now arrived from Credit: Getty

Giovanni Leoni - Liverpool

The Italian defender snubbed interest from other Premier League clubs to complete a £26m move to Anfield last summer.

Leoni was given the perfect billing upon his arrival, having been tipped to become the long-term replacement for Virgil van Dijk.

After much fanfare, the 19-year-old started to impress on his Reds debut against Southampton in the Carabao Cup in September.

However, Leoni left the field on a stretcher and was later revealed to have sustained an ACL injury that immediately ended his season.

The former Parma starlet is now close to returning to full training and is expected to play a part in pre-season under Andoni Iraola.

And it couldn't be more timely for Liverpool, who saw centre-back Ibrahima Konate leave on a free transfer to Real Madrid in June.

8 Liverpool fans have seen £26m man Leoni play for the club just once Credit: Getty

Stefan Bajcetic - Liverpool

New Reds boss Iraola may be even more excited at the prospect of his Spanish compatriot finally putting his injury woes behind him.

Still only 21, Bajcetic looked to be the future of Liverpool's midfield after bursting onto the scene under Jurgen Klopp in 2022/23.

He became the youngest Liverpool player to start a Champions League knockout match for the club in a 5-2 home loss to Real Madrid in February 2023.

Yet an adductor injury weeks later prematurely ended his breakthrough campaign, and started three years of fitness issues.

Liverpool's No.43 hasn't played for the club since May 2024, and hasn't featured at any level since undergoing a hamstring operation in May 2025 following a loan spell at Las Palmas.

But Bajcetic has been involved in Liverpool training again in Chicago, with Iraola optimistic of him returning to the pitch in pre-season.

8 Bajcetic has played just 97 minutes for Liverpool since first suffering injury problems in March 2023 Credit: Getty

Matthijs de Ligt - Manchester United

talkSPORT’s dedicated Man United show Inside Devils have urged the club to offload the £43m defender this summer.

However, De Ligt will be itching to prove he still has a part to play under Michael Carrick as he recovers from a back injury.

The 26-year-old's season came to an abrupt end in November, having played every minute of the first 13 Premier League games of last year.

The Netherlands international underwent successful surgery to fix his back issue in May and is expected to return in the early stages of United's 2026-27 season.

“Since November I have done everything, pushing myself in every session and exploring every option, to get back to doing what I love, playing football,” De Ligt said in a statement.

“I am grateful to everyone who has supported me throughout a difficult period in my career.

“I remain as determined as ever to represent Manchester United and play in front of our incredible supporters as soon as possible.”

8 De Ligt has been reduced to a mere spectator since the end of November Credit: Getty

Dejan Kulusevski - Tottenham

The Swede has not played at all since he suffered a patella injury in his right knee in Spurs' 2-0 defeat to Crystal Palace in May, 2025.

Kulusevski had been enjoying a fine individual campaign until then, with Glenn Hoddle naming him Tottenham's best player 'by a mile'.

But he missed the Europa League final win over Manchester United after undergoing surgery and has had numerous setbacks since.

Kulusevski claimed in March this year that he hoped to be back in action in time for Sweden's World Cup campaign.

The 26-year-old failed to recover in time, but Roberto De Zerbi issued a rare update on when fans could finally see him back in action.

“We have to see in the next couple of weeks,” De Zerbi said when asked about Kulusevski last week.

“He's another important player. After one season, one complete season, without a game, we have to analyse better and better, don't take risks, first of all for him and then for us.”

Sports.title: First goal of Xabi Alonso era scored by starlet who isn’t yet a Chelsea player
Sports.content:
First goal of Xabi Alonso era scored by starlet who isn’t yet a Chelsea player

Dastan Satpayev marked his unofficial Chelsea debut with a powerful strike just six minutes into a ten-goal pre-season friendly.

The Blues came from behind on three occasions to beat Western Sydney Wanderers 6-4 on Tuesday in their summer schedule opener.



3 Satpayev made a dream start to life at Chelsea, but is not officially their player just yet Credit: Getty

Joao Pedro, who has been resting amid his shock World Cup omission with Brazil, came off the bench to score a hat-trick in Sydney.

His fellow striker Satpayev also made a good impression on manager Xabi Alonso, even though he isn't technically a Chelsea player just yet.

Satpayev starts and scores in six

It was announced in February 2025 that the Kazakh starlet would join Chelsea this summer from FC Kairat for a reported €4million (£3.4m).



FIFA rules state that clubs can only complete international transfers if the player is aged 18 or above.

Chelsea and Kairat reached an agreement for Satpayev when he was 16-years-old, meaning he couldn't complete an immediate move.



However, with his 18th birthday approaching, he has been able to join his new club for pre-season as a trialist.

As per Peter Rutzler of The Times, Chelsea received permission from Kairat and the player's family to include him in their squad.



Satpayev was named in Alonso's starting XI to face Wanderers and managed to score the opening goal in style.

Academy star Ryan Kavuma-McQueen fed an excellent ball into the 17-year-old, who then blasted into the back of the net.

He played 63 minutes of the match before Alonso substituted him for Jamie Gittens.

3 Pedro came off the bench and scored a hat-trick in the wild win Credit: Getty



Satpayev has scored 26 goals in 58 matches for Kairat and netted in their debut Champions League campaign last season.

The teenager has also earned eight caps for Kazakhstan, for whom he made his debut aged just 16 in March 2025.

Chelsea up and running under Alonso

Minutes after Satpayev scored, Wanderers levelled via Anthony Pantazopoulos and then took the lead thansk to Aydan Hammond.

Dario Essugo made it 2-2 before the break, but Dylan Scicluna put the hosts back in front shortly after the hour mark.



Wanderers led yet again through Awan Lual after Gittens netted for Chelsea, who then wrapped it up with a stunning Pedro performance.

Although they conceded four goals, the Blues made a winning start to life under Alonso.

3 Alonso has got his first taste of victory in the Chelsea hotseat Credit: Getty

Satpayev and Marco Palestra were the only new signings to feature for the west Londoners amid a swathe of young talent.



Chelsea return to action on Saturday when they face Premier League rivals Tottenham Hotspur in their second friendly.

Sports.title: Ex-Arsenal star Takehiro Tomiyasu training with Premier League side after playing just nine games with Ajax
Sports.content:
Ex-Arsenal star Takehiro Tomiyasu training with Premier League side after playing just nine games with Ajax

Ex-Arsenal defender Takehiro Tomiyasu is training with Crystal Palace after becoming a free agent, talkSPORT understands.

The Japan international is currently without a club, having left Ajax following the expiry of his contract at the end of the 2025/26.

5 Tomiyasu is looking for a new club after spending the first part of his summer at the World Cup with Japan Credit: Getty

Tomiyasu joined Ajax in December after mutually agreeing to end his contract with Arsenal last summer.

The 28-year-old signed for the Dutch giants whilst still recovering from a long-term knee injury that had kept him out of action for almost a year prior.

But having only penned a six-month deal until the end of the season, Tomiyasu ultimately departed having made just nine appearances.

Now, after making three appearances for Japan in their run to the last-32 of the 2026 World Cup, he has begun pre-season despite not yet having found a new club.

An Eagle has landed?

Tomiyasu has joined up with with Crystal Palace this week as they get their season's preparations underway in Como, Italy.

While reports claim that the full-back is targeting a return to the Premier League, talkSPORT understands any talk of him joining the Eagles is premature.

With a number of Palace's first-team stars yet to report back for training after the World Cup, they have offered Tomiyasu a place to train and work on his fitness ahead of the new season.

This is understood to have been facilitated by his friendship with Palace midfielder and fellow Japan international, Daichi Kamada.

According to the Athletic, Tomiyasu could feature for the Premier League side in a friendly later this week.

But talkSPORT understands no discussions have been held over the ex-Gunners star joining the club, while he continues to attract interest from elsewhere in England and Europe.

5 Tomiyasu was a fan favourite at Arsenal, despite being heavily affected by injury Credit: Getty

5 Pierre Sage is looking to make his mark at Conference League winners Crystal Palace Credit: Getty

Crystal Palace are currently gearing up for their first season under new boss Pierre Sage, who was named as Oliver Glasner's successor in June.

They are in the market for a new defender as key man Maxence Lacroix looks set to join Chelsea in a deal worth £55m.

talkSPORT understands Palace are considering Augsburg’s Chrislain Matsima as a potential replacement, while Tomiyasu himself is capable of playing at centre-back.

Fresh start

Tomiyasu is looking to get his career back on track after seeing his last few seasons blighted by injury.

He departed Arsenal in July 2025 following the mutual decision to terminate his contract a year early, and had not featured for the club since the previous October.

The Japan star had missed the start of the 2024/25 season due to a previous knee injury that needed surgery in 2023.

5 Tomiyasu featured in just one game in his final season at Arsenal due to a knee injury Credit: Getty

But another knee issue saw him go under the knife again in January 2025, ultimately leading to his early departure from north London.

Tomiyasu joined Arsenal from Serie A side Bologna in a deal rising to £20million in 2021, and featured 84 times overall, scoring two goals and providing two assists.

After joining Ajax in December last year, he made his debut in January, but only eight further appearances followed.

The ex-Premier League star ultimately played only 236 minutes of football, failing to earn a new contract as the Amsterdam outfit finished a disappointing fifth in the Eredivisie.

Following his departure, Tomiyasu penned an emotional statement, where he shared his sadness at not having played a bigger role.

He wrote on Instagram: “It was only five months but I would like to thank all who support Ajax.

5 Tomiyasu hadn't started a league game for any club in almost two seasons before his full Ajax debut in March Credit: Getty

“Obviously it was not the season we wanted and no one is satisfied with how it ended.

“Personally, I joined this club in January after such a long rehab, I wanted to give much more, I should have done much more for this club but it didn’t work out well."

Sports.title: Chelsea star leaves pre-season tour to return to UK amid transfer speculation
Sports.content:
Filip Jorgensen has left Chelsea's pre-season tour of Australia, talkSPORT understands.

The goalkeeper has returned to the United Kingdom amid growing transfer interest.



3 Jorgensen has left Chelsea's pre-season tour amid growing transfer interest Credit: Getty

Jorgensen had been part of the Blues' squad for their trip to Australia and Asia.

However, he departed the camp ahead of Wednesday's opening match against Western Sydney Wanderers.

Chelsea will also face Tottenham Hotspur on Saturday in Australia before fixtures against Juventus, AC Milan and Malaysian champions Johor Darul Ta'zim.



Transfer interest

talkSPORT understands Strasbourg are currently interested in signing Jorgensen this summer.

Meanwhile, Coventry City have also made an approach for the Denmark international.



The Sky Blues remain confident of re-signing Carl Rushworth to be their goalkeeper this season, though.

Rushworth spent last season on loan from Brighton as Frank Lampard's side won promotion to the Premier League as champions.



Coventry have seen two bids rejected by the Seagulls already this summer, with their latest offer worth £25million.

Brighton are understood to be holding out for closer to £30million for the former England under-21 international.

As for Jorgensen, he failed to secure a move away from Stamford Bridge in January.

3 Strasbourg and Coventry have both shown interest in signing Jorgensen this summer Credit: Getty



Of his 12 appearances in all competitions last season, only five came in the league.

The 24-year-old, who signed from Villarreal in 2024, currently has five years left on his Chelsea contract.

Since joining the Blues, he has won both the Conference League and Club World Cup.

Jorgensen has also kept 11 clean sheets and conceded just 39 goals in his 36 total appearances for the club.



Chelsea goalkeeping options

Xabi Alonso's squad still contains three goalkeepers, despite Jorgensen's departure from their pre-season tour.

First-choice stopper Robert Sanchez is joined in Australia by youngsters Teddy Sharman-Lowe and Ted Curd.

3 Sanchez remains Chelsea's first-choice goalkeeper ahead of the new season Credit: Getty

Their goalkeeping ranks will also be boosted by Mike Penders later this summer following his loan spell at Strasbourg last term.



Penders was part of the Belgium squad which reached the quarter-finals of the World Cup.

Sports.title: Where to watch Manchester United v Atletico Madrid plus UK kick-off time, squads and location
Sports.content:
Where to watch Manchester United v Atletico Madrid plus UK kick-off time, squads and location

Manchester United will take their pre-season up a notch on Saturday afternoon, as they face Atletico Madrid in Stockholm.

Michael Carrick's side have made a mixed start to their friendlies in Scandinavia, as they were first beaten 1-0 by Championship Wrexham, before thumping Rosenborg 5-0 in Norway.



4 A youthful Manchester United side thumped Rosenborg in their second pre-season test Credit: Getty

The youngsters put on a show for the Red Devils in their latest outing, with Shea Lacey, Jacob Devaney, Harry Amass and Ethan Williams all getting on the scoresheet, as well as Joshua Zirkzee.

Now, United face their toughest test of pre-season yet, as they head to Sweden to face Champions League semi-finalists Atletico Madrid.

This will give fans a real insight into preparations ahead of their first full season under Carrick, whose side are gearing up for their return among Europe's elite after a third-place Premier League finish.



They will be hoping for a strong showing against Atletico, before an even bigger test against European champions Paris Saint-Germain.

United's Premier League campaign will then start on Saturday, August 22 as they face a trip to take on newly-promoted side Hull City, live on talkSPORT.



Where to watch Manchester United vs Atletico Madrid

This pre-season fixture will be played on Saturday, August 1.

The friendly is going to be played at the Strawberry Arena in Stockholm, Sweden with kick-off set for 2pm UK time.

Fans will be able to watch the game live from the UK too.

Subscribers to MUTV can tune in to the action on TV, on their app, or online via Man United's official website.



talkSPORT and talkSPORT.com will also be across all the latest.

4 Diego Simeone is gearing up for his fifteenth season in charge of Atletico Credit: Getty

Listen talkSPORT through the website or find us on DAB digital radio through your smart speaker and on 1089 or 1053 AM.

Download and listen to all our live commentaries via the talkSPORT app.

For the latest odds and bet boosts for every big event, visit talkSPORT BET.



Subscribe to the talkSPORT YouTube channel for news, views and analysis plus our regular goals show and for more, 

Manchester United vs Atletico Madrid: Squads

Bruno Fernandes remains one of the stars not yet back with United due to an extended break after the World Cup.

Matheus Cunha, Noussair Mazraoui and Altay Bayindir are also yet to return to training, as well as Marcus Rashford and Kobbie Mainoo.

4 Bruno Fernandes is yet to return to Man United, after his World Cup round of 16 exit with Portugal Credit: Getty



Meanwhile, Benjamin Sesko and new arrival Karl Darlow did not travel with the Red Devils squad to Norway for the win against Rosenborg, but both are expected to be fit for the start of the season.

As for Atletico Madrid, their clash with United will be just their second pre-season fixture after they face Getafe on Wednesday, with a number of their first-team squad still to return from the World Cup.

This includes victorious Spain stars Marcos Llorente, Marc Pubill, Alex Baena and Alejandro Grimaldo, as well as six of Argentina's beaten finalists - Julian Alvarez, Giuliano Simeone, Nahuel Molina, Juan Musso, Nico Gonzalez and Thiago Almada.

Manchester United pre-season squad

Goalkeepers: Tom Heaton, Radek Vitek, Dermot Mee.

Defenders: Harry Maguire, Patrick Dorgu, Leny Yoro, Luke Shaw, Ayden Heaven, Harry Amass, Jaydan Kamason, Dan Armer.



Midfielders: Mason Mount, Andrey Santos, Jack Fletcher, Tyler Fletcher, Toby Collyer, Dan Gore, Jacob Devaney, Jim Thwaites.

Forwards: Joshua Zirkzee, Bryan Mbeumo, Chido Obi, Ethan Wheatley, Shea Lacey, Ethan Williams, JJ Gabriel.

Atletico Madrid pre-season squad

Goalkeepers: Jan Oblak

Defenders: Matteo Ruggeri, David Hancko, Robin Le Normand, Jose Maria Gimenez

Midfielders: Thomas Lemar, Morten Hjulmand, Rodrigo Mendoza, Koke, Pablo Barrios



Forwards: Carlos Martin, Ademola Lookman

4 Michael Carrick is currently overseeing his pre-season as Man United boss Credit: Getty

Manchester United vs Atletico Madrid: What has been said?

Carrick hailed his team's progress in pre-season, as they bounced back from defeat to Wrexham to thump Rosenborg.

Speaking afterwards, the Man United boss said: “It’s important to build through this pre-season, some players need more minutes than others as they go and we’re managing some players a little bit more than others.

"I've said it before the game, it's never going to be perfect, two weeks in and you're kind of building towards that.



"So, I thought there was a lot of good things, some of the goals were fantastic goals and it’s just as pleasing to keep a clean sheet.

"So yeah, we’re moving forward nicely.”

Sports.title: Aston Villa have teenage phenom likened to Romelu Lukaku but he’s banned from playing until January
Sports.content:
Aston Villa have teenage phenom likened to Romelu Lukaku but he’s banned from playing until January

Brian Madjo has always stood out, literally and figuratively.

At just 17 years of age, Madjo is 193cm tall and already appears to have the physical strength of an ox.

6 It's hard to miss Madjo on the pitch Credit: Getty



Aston Villa fans got their first glimpse of Madjo's imposing build in their first pre-season friendly against Walsall, which they won 5-0.

Madjo, who started the contest up top, scored twice.

His first goal showcased his strength, fending off his marker to get on the end of Kosta Nedeljkovic's cross from the right and slam a first-time finish into the net.

Madjo's second came when Emi Buendia's attempt on goal smacked him in the head, only to re-gather his composure and smash it home.

Although it was slightly fortuitous, Madjo's intelligent movement in the lead-up ensured he was in the right place at the right time, proving he is equal parts brain and brawn.



Madjo's display set tongues wagging among Villa fans given it was their first proper glimpse of the striker who joined from FC Metz in January for an estimated £10million.

The two key challenges that accelerated Madjo's rise

But Madjo shining against players older than him shouldn't have come as a surprise.



In fact, during Madjo's time in Luxembourg club Racing Union's academy, he never played against kids his own age.

Instead, he played two age groups higher to challenge him physically and mentally.



But that wasn't even the trickiest part of his development.

6 Madjo is highly rated within Villa Credit: Getty

"The thing is, physically he was always big and strong and fast," Racing Union academy director Delvin Skenderovic told talkSPORT.com.

"The problem we had to work on was his technique, his behaviour under pressure.

"So what we used to do in some games, we put him as a midfielder where he had more pressure in his back to improve his technical skills, to learn how to behave with pressure, to learn to keep the ball.



"We could have put him as a striker and he would score two or three goals every match, but this was not the point.

"The point was his development and this was a point we had to work on."

Madjo was already on Racing Union's books when Skenderovic joined the club five years ago.

6 Madjo already was a physical presence during his early teenage years Credit: Racing Union



6 Madjo was on Racing Union's books until 2023, when he moved to Metz Credit: Racing Union

But Skenderovic, along with just about everyone at the club, quickly recognised Madjo 'will be a big thing'.

"Brian is a kid with an elite mentality," Skenderovic continued.

"He's always working on himself. He always wants to improve."

Unmistakable Madjo comparison spells danger for rival defenders

Given Madjo's physical build coupled with his nose for goal, fans have been quick to draw comparisons between the teenager and a certain Belgian beast.

Even Skenderovic believes Madjo boasts a similar profile to the player, but there's one key area of his game that sets the Villa prodigy apart.



"I think he reminds me a lot of Romelu Lukaku," Skenderovic said.

6 Lukaku has been named in both the Serie A and Premier League teams of the year Credit: Getty

"I think he has quite a similar profile where he's able to keep the ball, he's strong with his head.

"But I just think Brian will be a little bit faster than Lukaku."

Given Lukaku has scored over 300 goals throughout his senior professional career and 93 at international level for Belgium, replicating even half of that will be no easy task for Madjo.

Why can't Madjo play for Villa until January?

Unfortunately for the teenager, it may be another six months before he can start accumulating goals as a senior Villa player.



Because Madjo was signed from an overseas club before he turned 18, FIFA rejected Villa's attempt to register him, pointing to Article 19 of their regulations which stipulate international transfers of players under the age of 18 are prohibited.

What makes the situation all the more frustrating for Villa is that Madjo was born in England and has represented the nation at Under-17 level.

6 Emery won't be able to let Madjo loose unless a CAS ruling goes in Villa's favour Credit: Getty

Villa have since appealed FIFA's decision to block Madjo's registration and escalated their case to the Court of Arbitration for Sport (CAS), with a verdict yet to be handed down.



Yet even if Madjo is forced to wait until he turns 18 on January 12 to play for Villa, Skenderovic does not believe it will impact his trajectory as he's fully convinced by the teen's talent.

"Honestly, I see Brian in a couple of years in the best European clubs," Skenderovic said.

"I think he has a very good profile to adapt in the Premier League, which, for me, is the hardest league in the world.

"I think he can go to the top."

Sports.title: Village cricket cheating scandal convulses Middle England as 'Clicky Ponting' fielder's trick fools umpires
Sports.content:
A village cricket scandal has gone viral across the world... by the very literal click of a finger. An investigation has been launched after a cheating storm - fuelled by viral social media video evidence - engulfed English grassroots cricket. Its focus is Saltburn Cricket Club in North Yorkshire after online footage appeared to show a slip fielder fooling umpires by clicking his fingers to imitate the sound of an edge off the bat. Multiple videos suggest it has been happening for some time. Footage from Saltburn's 2nd XI match with Norton Cricket Club in Division Two of the North Yorkshire and South Durham League last weekend showed a ball delivered by Saltburn bowler Sam Morrison passing the bat of Norton batsman Noman Shabir without making contact with it. At the same time, Saltburn slip fielder - who Daily Mail Sport understands is Brian Devine - seems to click his fingers. When Saltburn wicketkeeper Josh Bowes takes the ball, Saltburn appeal and the umpire gives Shabir out. Shabir can clearly be seen objecting to his dismissal and seems to indicate to the umpire that he did not hit the ball and that the noise heard was a clicking of fingers instead. Amateur cricket player Brian Devine has been caught appearing to click his fingers to make it appear that a batter has been caught behind when in fact they haven't hit the ball at all Saltburn player has been caught on camera clicking his fingers whenever ball was near bat Norton batsman Noman Shabir protested that he didn't touch the ball after being given out Devine has been dubbed as 'Clicky Ponting' on social media for his actions on the cricket field The clip and other similar evidence have attracted international media attention and gone viral online and on social media. A statement from the North Yorkshire and South Durham League read: 'The League has received a formal complaint regarding alleged incidents in a Division Two game on Saturday 25th July 2026. A full investigation has been initiated and until such time as the formal processes are complete, no further comment will be made.' Saltburn won their match with Norton by a mammoth 159 runs. Devine has been dubbed 'Clicky Ponting' - in a light-hearted reference to Australia legend Ricky Ponting. That's as far as the funny side goes though with the likes of Piers Morgan condemning the actions. Taking to X, the avid cricket fan wrote: 'Outrageous cheating, and just the tip of the iceberg from all that's come out since it was exposed. 'Clicky Ponting (as he is now known) and various teammates at Saltburn CC, have clearly been at this shameful scam for years. Imagine doing this in local amateur cricket? Pathetic.' Other clips online appear to show Devine clicking his fingers to cheat umpires and earn dismissals unfairly in other matches. One such example is a video showing footage of a match between Saltburn and Middlesbrough second XI.

Sports.title: Nine-minute hat-trick hero Joao Pedro is 'very hungry' after Brazil World Cup snub, says Xabi Alonso - as Chelsea boss opens up on Danny Welbeck and Jordan Henderson pursuits
Sports.content:
Nine-minute hat-trick hero Joao Pedro is 'very hungry' after Brazil World Cup snub, says Xabi Alonso - as Chelsea boss opens up on Danny Welbeck and Jordan Henderson pursuits

See more Daily Mail on Google - save us as a Preferred Source

Xabi Alonso described Joao Pedro as ‘very hungry’ after Chelsea’s striker scored a nine-minute hat-trick in Sydney, having been left at home by Brazil boss Carlo Ancelotti for the World Cup.

The 24-year-old was surprisingly ignored by Ancelotti this summer, and in a friendly win over Western Sydney Wanderers, he replaced Liam Delap while his side were trailing 3-2.

Joao Pedro assisted Jamie Gittens for the equaliser before scoring three times himself for a 6-4 victory.

‘He is very hungry,’ Alonso said when asked about Joao Pedro being snubbed by Brazil. ‘Joao is really, really determined to have a great season. He wants to keep scoring more and more.

'We need to help him. On his own it's not possible. He will have the players around him. It’s not just about the striker, but every time we win and our striker scores, I am happy.’

On Delap, who could leave this summer to make way for Danny Welbeck, the 35-year-old at Brighton who Daily Mail Sport revealed is a transfer target, Alonso added: ‘I see him in a good mood, in a good desire to get proper fitness, proper football, feeling good, and he's doing well.’

Joao Pedro scored a hat-trick as Chelsea beat Western Sydney Wanderers 6-4 in pre-season

Blues boss Xabi Alonso said the striker is 'very hungry' after missing the World Cup with Brazil

Asked about wanting to add experience, with Chelsea looking at Welbeck and Brentford midfielder Jordan Henderson, 36, Alonso said: ‘Everyone has to learn. Everyone. It doesn't matter if you are young, if you are more experienced, this is what happens in the game.

‘This is a quality as well that you need. You can be quick. You can be good at dribbling. But you can have this game intelligence to do the things and from everything we need to be quick because the competition is in just almost a month and we want to get ready for that.

‘We want to have a complete squad and we want to make a good team. For that we have an idea, we have a plan, and let's see how we set it up until the start of the Premier League.’

Asked specifically about Welbeck, Alonso said: ‘No comment.’

Romeo Lavia received no minutes in this friendly because of a minor hamstring issue. In his place, 16-year-old Reggie Watson was the only player to complete a full 90 for Chelsea, and the son of former Crystal Palace and Wigan footballer Ben impressed in the centre.

As did Dastan Satpayev, the 17-year-old who arrived this summer from Kazakhstan side FC Kairat. ‘He is really strong, really quick, and you will be really impressed with him,’ Alonso said.

Sports.title: Newcastle insist Arsenal have NOT made approach for Bruno Guimaraes, Nottingham Forest among list of clubs targeting Chelsea's Liam Delap... and Ajax want return for West Ham's Edson Alvarez: WINDOW WATCH
Sports.content:
It's that time of the year again - the transfer window is now open until September 1 and it's sure to be a busy period with clubs looking to make big signings ahead of next season.

Here are today's latest developments from Simon Jones and the Daily Mail Sport team...

Tomiyasu training with Palace

Former Arsenal defender Takehiro Tomiyasu is training with Crystal Palace after the expiry of his contract at Ajax.

The Japan international was expected to extend his contract but is a free agent after making just nine appearances since moving to Amsterdam on a short-term deal in January owing in part to a hamstring injury.

The 27-year-old is training with Palace in Como as part of the club’s pre-season preparations and could feature in a friendly this week. He has had interest from Venezia and Sassuolu, too.

Palace are playing in the Como Cup. They face Lens, new manager Pierre Sage's former side, tonight then take on Famalicao in two 45-minute games.

Takehiro Tomiyasu

Bees eye Sarr signing

Brentford are weighing up a move for Tottenham midfielder Pape Matar Sarr.

The Bees were looking to strengthen their options even before news of Jordan Henderson's proposed departure for Chelsea.

They remain in talks over 18-year-old Ousmane Diabate from Genclirbirligi, amid competition from Spurs, but the teenager is regarded as one for the future. They now want two more for the first team squad with Henderson heading towards Stamford Bridge.

Sarr, 23, has had interest from Turkey but would be open to remaining in London if, as it seems, his first team starting chances will be limited following Spurs' purchase of Sandro Tonali and Mateus Fernandes.

Pape Matar Sarr is on Brentford's radar, with Jordan Henderson wanted by Chelsea

Newcastle still waiting on Arsenal bid for Bruno

Newcastle United insist they have still to receive a formal approach from Arsenal for midfielder Bruno Guimaraes.

Arsenal have been preparing to make an official £70m-plus move for the Brazilian who is keen to join them but, so far, Newcastle sources say any proposals have come via the player's agent.

Newcastle manager Eddie Howe said at the weekend he was unsure what would happen over the 28-year-old's future.

Bruno Guimaraees wants to move to Arsenal but Newcastle say they are still waiting for a bid

Delap in demand with Chelsea set to sign Welbeck

Nottingham Forest remain among the list of clubs showing interest in Chelsea striker Liam Delap.

Danny Welbeck's pending arrival from Brighton is likely to leave fewer opportunities for 22-year-old Delap and clubs are enquiring to ascertain the deal required to sign the former Ipswich Town forward.

Forest, Everton and Newcastle United are just some of the clubs who have expressed interest in the former England U21 international.

Meanwhile, Forest have made an offer for Union Saint-Gilloise full-back Anan Khalaili as talks for Feyenoord's Givairo Read also continue.

Both players are also appreciated by Bournemouth and Newcastle United.

Liam Delap is a target for several clubs with his chances at Chelsea likely to be limited

Jorgensen leaves camp for France

Chelsea goalkeeper Filip Jorgensen has left their camp in Australia ahead of joining sister club Strasbourg.

The 24-year-old Denmark international made 12 appearances for Chelsea last season and wants regular first team football.

On my Edson! Ajax want West Ham's Alvarez back

Ajax are trying to re-sign West Ham midfielder Edson Alvarez.

The Dutch side sold Alvarez to West Ham for £35million in 2023 and now hope to buy him back.

West Ham want around £12.5m but Ajax sources say they are still owed money from the way payment was structured on the original transfer.

The 28-year-old, who has spoken to Ajax director Jordi Cruyff, spent last season on loan at Fenerbahce and was part of Mexico's World Cup squad but has generally struggled to live up to expectations since leaving Amsterdam.

Real Sociedad are also interested in Alvarez but are proposing a smaller, structured deal.

Edson Alvarez in action for Mexico against England at the World Cup

Rock on Tommi to Meadow Lane

Aston Villa winger Tommi O'Reilly is in talks to join League One Notts County on loan.

The 22-year-old had been set to sign for Sheffield Wednesday but, after further discussions, Villa have decided Meadow Lane may suit his development better.

O'Reilly had an outstanding campaign with Crewe last season and Villa hope he can replicate that form under Notts County coach Martin Paterson.

Notts County also signed Australian forward Luka Smyth from Finnish top-flight side VPS yesterday for an undisclosed fee on a three-year deal.

Notts County are in talks over a deal for Villa's Tommi O'Reilly

Perri set for Italian job after Trafford deal

Leeds United goalkeeper Lucas Perri is expected to join Torino on loan with an option to buy once a deal for James Trafford is completed.

Trafford, 23, is poised to sign a deal worth around £130,000 a week once Manchester City and Leeds finalise details on an expected £40m transfer with £5m in add-ons and a sell-on clause.

Torino and Leeds have agreed an initial loan move for Perri for the coming season. The deal also includes an option to buy him permanently next summer.

Leeds goalkeepers Karl Darlow and Illan Meslier have left Daniel Farke’s squad to join Manchester United and Arsenal this summer.

They would still like another as cover as well as strengthening at left-back, attacking midfield and striker.

Lucas Perri's Torino deal may be signed off after James Trafford arrives from Manchester City
